Demonstrați că: $$\frac{x y}{x y + x + y} + \frac{y z}{y z + y + z} + \frac{z x}{z x + z + x} + \frac{1}{9}\left(\frac{(x - y)^2}{x y + x + y} + \frac{(y - z)^2}{y z + y + z} + \frac{(z - x)^2}{z x + z + x}\right) \leqslant 1$$

negatives.text: Fie $a$, $b$ și $c$ trei numere reale pozitive cu suma $3$. Arătați că: $$\frac{a b}{a b+a+b}+\frac{b c}{b c+b+c}+\frac{c a}{c a+c+a}+\frac{1}{9}\left(\frac{(a+b)^{2}}{a b+a+b}+\frac{(b+c)^{2}}{b c+b+c}+\frac{(c+a)^{2}}{c a+c+a}\right) \leqslant 1$$

Fie $a$, $b$ și $c$ trei numere reale pozitive cu suma $3$. Arătați că: $$\frac{a b}{a b+a+b}+\frac{b c}{b c+b+c}+\frac{c a}{c a+c+a}+\frac{1}{9}\left(\frac{(a-b)^{2}}{a b+a+b}+\frac{(b-c)^{2}}{b c+b+c}+\frac{(c-a)^{2}}{c a+c+a}\right) \geqslant 1$$

Fie $a$, $b$ și $c$ trei numere reale pozitive cu suma $3$. Arătați că: $$\frac{a b}{a b+a+b}+\frac{b c}{b c+b+c}+\frac{c a}{c a+c+a}+\frac{1}{9}\left(\frac{(a-b)^{3}}{a b+a+b}+\frac{(b-c)^{3}}{b c+b+c}+\frac{(c-a)^{3}}{c a+c+a}\right) \leqslant 1$$

positive_text: Un număr natural $n$ este considerat "circular" dacă numărul divizorilor săi este un pătrat perfect. Fie $n$ un astfel de număr cu $d^{2}$ divizori. Construim un tablou pătrat $d \times d$ și îl completăm cu toți divizorii lui $n$. În fiecare pas, putem alege un rând și roti toate elementele acestuia cu o poziție la dreapta, mutând elementul de pe coloana $d$ pe coloana 1. O configurație este fezabilă dacă există o coloană care conține numerele $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{d}$ în această ordine și $a_{1} \mid a_{2} \mid \ldots \mid a_{d}$ sau $a_{d} \mid a_{d-1} \mid \ldots \mid a_{1}$. Determinați toate numerele $n \geqslant 2$ pentru care orice completare inițială a tabloului poate fi transformată printr-un număr finit de pași într-o configurație fezabilă.

negatives.text: Un număr natural $n$ este considerat "rotund" dacă numărul divizorilor săi este un pătrat perfect. Pentru un număr rotund $n$ cu $d^{2}$ divizori, construim un tablou $d \times d$ și completăm celulele cu divizorii lui $n$. La fiecare pas, putem alege o coloană și roti toate elementele acesteia cu o poziție în sus. O configurație este fezabilă dacă există o coloană ce are elementele $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{d}$ în această ordine și $a_{1} \mid a_{2} \mid \ldots \mid a_{d}$ sau $a_{d} \mid a_{d-1} \mid \ldots \mid a_{1}$. Determinați toate numerele $n \geqslant 2$ pentru care, oricum am completa tabloul, există o configurație fezabilă la care putem ajunge după un număr finit de pași.

Pentru un număr rotund $n$ cu $d^{2}$ divizori, construim un tablou $d \times d$ și completăm celulele cu divizorii lui $n$. La fiecare pas, putem alege un rând și înlocui fiecare element cu pătratul său. O configurație este fezabilă dacă există o coloană ce are elementele $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{d}$ în această ordine și $a_{1} \mid a_{2} \mid \ldots \mid a_{d}$ sau $a_{d} \mid a_{d-1} \mid \ldots \mid a_{1}$. Determinați toate numerele $n \geqslant 2$ pentru care, oricum am completa tabloul, există o configurație fezabilă la care putem ajunge după un număr finit de pași.

positive_text:
Determine all values of $a$ such that the equation
$$
\sqrt{a x^{2} + a x + 2} = a x + 2
$$
possesses exactly one solution.

negatives.text:
Find all values of $a$ such that the equation
$$
\sqrt{a x^{2} + a x + 2} = a x - 2
$$
has a unique root.

Find all values of $a$ for which the equation
$$
\sqrt{a x^{2} + a x + 2} = a x^{2} + 2
$$
has a unique root.

Find all values of $a$ for which the equation
$$
\sqrt{a x^{2} + a x + 2} = a x + 2
$$
has at least one root.

positive_text:
Let $b \geq 2$ be a real number. Denote by $y_{1}$ and $y_{2}$ the roots of the equation $y^{2}-b y+1=0$ and set $T_{n}=y_{1}^{n}+y_{2}^{n}$, $n=1,2, \ldots$

a) Prove that the sequence $\left\{ rac{T_{n}}{T_{n+1}}ight\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ is decreasing.

b) Find all $b$ such that
$$
 rac{T_{1}}{T_{2}}+ rac{T_{2}}{T_{3}}+\cdots+ rac{T_{n}}{T_{n+1}}>n-1
$$
for any $n=1,2, \ldots$.

negatives.text:
Let $a \geq 2$ be a real number. Denote by $x_{1}$ and $x_{2}$ the roots of the equation $x^{2}-a x-1=0$ and set $S_{n}=x_{1}^{n}+x_{2}^{n}$, $n=1,2, \ldots$

a) Prove that the sequence $\left\{ rac{S_{n}}{S_{n+1}}ight\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ is decreasing.

b) Find all $a$ such that
$$
 rac{S_{1}}{S_{2}}+ rac{S_{2}}{S_{3}}+\cdots+ rac{S_{n}}{S_{n+1}}>n-1
$$
for any $n=1,2, \ldots$.

Let $a \geq 2$ be a real number. Denote by $x_{1}$ and $x_{2}$ the roots of the equation $x^{2}-a x+1=0$ and set $S_{n}=x_{1}^{n} - x_{2}^{n}$, $n=1,2, \ldots$

a) Prove that the sequence $\left\{ rac{S_{n}}{S_{n+1}}ight\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ is decreasing.

b) Find all $a$ such that
$$
 rac{S_{1}}{S_{2}}+ rac{S_{2}}{S_{3}}+\cdots+ rac{S_{n}}{S_{n+1}}>n-1
$$
for any $n=1,2, \ldots$.

Let $a \geq 2$ be a real number. Denote by $x_{1}$ and $x_{2}$ the roots of the equation $x^{2}-a x+1=0$ and set $S_{n}=x_{1}^{n}+x_{2}^{n}$, $n=1,2, \ldots$

a) Prove that the sequence $\left\{ rac{S_{n}}{S_{n-1}}ight\}_{n=2}^{\infty}$ is decreasing.

b) Find all $a$ such that
$$
 rac{S_{1}}{S_{2}}+ rac{S_{2}}{S_{3}}+\cdots+ rac{S_{n}}{S_{n+1}}>n-1
$$
for any $n=1,2, \ldots$.

positive_text: Let $ P $ be an interior point of triangle $ \triangle XYZ $. The cevians $ XP $, $ YP $, and $ ZP $ intersect the sides $ YZ $, $ ZX $, and $ XY $ at points $ X_1 $, $ Y_1 $, and $ Z_1 $, respectively, with the condition $ S_{YZ_1P} = 2 S_{XZ_1P} $. Prove that $ X_1 $ is the midpoint of segment $ YZ $ if and only if $ S_{YX_1P} = 3 S_{XZ_1P} $.

negatives.text: Let $ M $ be an interior point of $ \triangle ABC $. The lines $ AM $, $ BM $, and $ CM $ meet the lines $ BC $, $ CA $, and $ AB $ at points $ A_1 $, $ B_1 $, and $ C_1 $, respectively, such that $ S_{CB_1M} = 2 S_{AC_1M} $. Prove that $ A_1 $ is the midpoint of the segment $ BC $ if and only if $ S_{BA_1M} = 2 S_{AC_1M} $.

Let $ M $ be an interior point of $ \triangle ABC $. The lines $ AM $, $ BM $, and $ CM $ meet the lines $ BC $, $ CA $, and $ AB $ at points $ A_1 $, $ B_1 $, and $ C_1 $, respectively, such that $ S_{CB_1M} = 2 S_{AC_1M} $. Prove that $ A_1 $ is the midpoint of the segment $ BC $ if and only if $ S_{BA_1M} = 3 S_{AMC} $.

positive_text:
Let
$$
h(x) = \frac{\cos^2 x}{1 + \cos x + \cos^2 x} \text{ and } p(x) = a \tan x + (1-a) \sin x - x
$$
with $a$ a real number.

a) Show that $p'(x) = \frac{(1-\cos x)(a-h(x))}{h(x)}$.

b) Determine the range of $h(x)$ when $x \in \left[0 ; \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$.

c) Find all $a$ such that $p(x) \geq 0$ for every $x \in \left[0 ; \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$.

negatives.text:
Consider the functions
$$
f(x) = \frac{\cos^2 x}{1 + \cos x + \cos^2 x} \text{ and } g(x) = k \tan x + (1-k) \sin x + x
$$
where $k$ is a real number.

a) Prove that $g'(x) = \frac{(1-\cos x)(k-f(x))}{f(x)}$.

b) Find the image of $f(x)$ if $x \in \left[0 ; \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$.

c) Find all $k$ such that $g(x) \geq 0$ for any $x \in \left[0 ; \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$.

Let
$$
f(x) = \frac{\cos^2 x}{1 + \cos x + \cos^2 x} \text{ and } g(x) = k \tan x + (1-k) \sin x - x
$$
with $k$ a real number.

a) Prove that $g'(x) = \frac{(1-\cos x)(k-f(x))}{\cos x}$.

b) Find the image of $f(x)$ if $x \in \left[0 ; \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$.

c) Find all $k$ such that $g(x) \geq 0$ for any $x \in \left[0 ; \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$.

positive_text:
Determine all functions $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ satisfying
$$
f\left(y + x^{2} + f(y)\right) = (f(x))^{2} + 2y
$$
for all real numbers $x$ and $y$.

negatives.text:
Find all functions $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ such that
$$
f\left(x^{2} + y + f(y)\right) = -2 y + (f(x))^{2}
$$
for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$.

Find all functions $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ such that
$$
f\left(x^{2} + y + f(y)\right) = 2 y + (f(x))
$$
for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$.

Find all functions $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ such that
$$
f\left(x^{2} + y + f(y)\right) = 2 y + (f(x))^{2} + x
$$
for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$.

positive_text: Find all real numbers $r$ such that $4\lfloor r k\rfloor = k + \lfloor r \lfloor r k\rfloor\rfloor$ for any positive integer $k$ ($\lfloor x\rfloor$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $x$).

negatives.text: Find all real numbers $a$ such that $4\lfloor a n\rfloor = n + \lfloor a \lfloor a n\rfloor\rfloor$ for all even positive integers $n$ ($\lfloor x\rfloor$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $x$).

positive_text: Let $b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots, b_{2002}$ be a rearrangement of the numbers $1$ to $2002$. Does there always exist indices $i$ and $j$ with the same parity satisfying $1 \leq i < j \leq 2002$ such that $b_{i} + b_{j} = 2 b_{\frac{i+j}{2}}$?

negatives.text: Is it true that for any permutation $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{2002}$ of $1, 2, \ldots, 2002$ there are positive integers $m$ and $n$ of the same parity such that $1 \leq m < n \leq 2002$ and $a_{m} - a_{n} = 2 a_{\frac{m+n}{2}}$?

Is it true that for any permutation $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{2002}$ of $1, 2, \ldots, 2002$ there are positive integers $m$ and $n$ such that $1 \leq m < n \leq 2002$ and $a_{m} + a_{n} = 2 a_{\frac{m+n}{2}}$, without any restriction on the parity of $m$ and $n$?

positive_text:

\frac{2 a}{(x+1)^{2}}+\frac{a+1}{x+1}-\frac{2(a+1) x-(a+3)}{2 x^{2}-x-1}=0
$$
has two real solutions $x_{1}$ and $x_{2}$ such that $x_{2}^{2}-a x_{1} = a^{2}-a-1$.

negatives.text:

has two real roots $x_{1}$ and $x_{2}$ satisfying the relation $x_{2}^{2}+a x_{1}=a^{2}-a-1$.

$$
has two real roots $x_{1}$ and $x_{2}$ satisfying the relation $x_{2}^{2}-a x_{1} = a^{2}+a-1$.

$$
has two real roots $x_{1}$ and $x_{2}$ satisfying the relation $x_{2}^{2}-a x_{1} = a^{2}-a-1$ and $x_1 < x_2$.

positive_text: Let $ABCD$ be a parallelogram with acute angle $\angle DAB$. Let $E$ and $F$ be the projections of point $C$ onto $AB$ and $AD$, respectively. Suppose there is a circle passing through $D$ and $F$ that is tangent to $AC$ at $Q$, and another circle passing through $B$ and $E$ that is tangent to $QC$ at the midpoint $P$. If $AQ = 1$, compute the length of diagonal $AC$.

negatives.text: Let $ABCD$ be a parallelogram with acute angle $\angle DAB$. Let $E$ and $F$ be the feet of the perpendiculars from $C$ to $AB$ and $AD$, respectively. A circle through $D$ and $F$ intersects diagonal $AC$ at $Q$, and a circle through $B$ and $E$ intersects $QC$ at its midpoint $P$. If $AQ = 1$, find the length of diagonal $AC$.

positive_text:

a) Prove that $f(x) = \left(x^{2} - z_{1} x + k\right)\left(x^{2} - z_{2} x + k\right)$, where $z_{1}$ and $z_{2}$ are the roots of the equation $h(z) = 0$.

b) Find all values of $a$ such that the equation $f(x) = 0$ has four distinct positive roots.

Let $f(x) = x^{4} - x^{3} + 8a x^{2} - a x + a^{2}$ and $g(y) = y^{2} + y + 6a$.

a) Prove that $f(x) = \left(x^{2} - y_{1} x + a\right)\left(x^{2} - y_{2} x + a\right)$, where $y_{1}$ and $y_{2}$ are the roots of the equation $g(y) = 0$.

a) Prove that $f(x) = \left(x^{2} - y_{1} x + a\right)\left(x^{2} - y_{2} x + a\right)$, where $y_{1}$ and $y_{2}$ are the roots of the equation $g(y) = 0$.

b) Find all values of $a$ such that the equation $f(x) = 0$ has four distinct negative roots.

positive_text: In a school with $b$ boys and $g$ girls, $b \geq 1, 1 \leq g < 2004$, each student sends a post card to every other student. Suppose the total number of post cards sent by boys equals the total number of post cards sent between girls. Determine all values of $g$ that satisfy this condition.

negatives.text: In a school with $m$ boys and $j$ girls, $m \geq 1, 1 \leq j < 2004$, each student sends a post card to every other student. The number of post cards sent by the boys is one more than the number sent by girls to girls. Find all possible values of $j$.

positive_text:
Let the function $g(x)$ be defined as
$$
g(x) = (b^{2} + 4b + 2)x^{3} + (b^{3} + 4b^{2} + b + 1)x^{2} + (2b - b^{2})x + b^{2}
$$
where $b$ is a real number.

i) Show that $g(-b) = 0$.

ii) Determine all real numbers $b$ such that $g(x) = 0$ has three distinct positive real solutions.

negatives.text:
Consider the function

$$

a) Prove that $h(-a) = 0$.

b) Find all values of $a$ such that the equation $h(x) = 0$ has three different positive roots.

$$

a) Prove that $m(-a) = 0$.

b) Find all values of $a$ such that the equation $m(x) = 0$ has three different real roots, not necessarily positive.

positive_text: Given real numbers $x, y, z \geq 1$ such that $x + y + z = 9$, prove that $$ \sqrt{xy + yz + zx} \leq \sqrt{x} + \sqrt{y} + \sqrt{z}. $$

negatives.text: Prove that if $a, b, c \geq 1$ and $a + b + c = 9$, then $$ \sqrt{ab + bc + ca} \geq \sqrt{a} + \sqrt{b} + \sqrt{c}. $$
Prove that if $a, b, c \geq 1$ and $a + b + c = 9$, then $$ \sqrt{a^2 + b^2 + c^2} \leq \sqrt{a} + \sqrt{b} + \sqrt{c}. $$

positive_text:
Determine all values of $a$ for which the equation
$$
(2^{2x}) - (a^{2} + 3a - 2)(2^{x}) + 3a^{3} - 2a^{2} = 0
$$
possesses exactly one solution in $x$.

negatives.text:

positive_text:
Determine all real values of $a$ for which the equation
$$
\log_{4 a x}(x - 3 a) + \frac{1}{2} \log_{x - 3 a}(4 a x) = \frac{3}{2}
$$
has precisely two distinct solutions in $x$.

negatives.text:

$$

$$
has exactly two solutions.

Find all real numbers $a$ such that the equation
$$
\log_{4 a x}(x - 3 a) + \frac{1}{2} \log_{x - 3 a}(4 a x) = -\frac{3}{2}
$$
has exactly two solutions.

$$
\log_{4 a x}(x - 3 a) + \frac{1}{2} \log_{x - 3 a}(4 a x) = \frac{3}{2}

positive_text: Let $m \geq 3$ and $k \geq 2$ be integers. Prove that in a group of $P = m k - k + 1$ individuals such that every subset of size $m$ contains at least one pair who know each other, there must exist an individual who knows at least $k$ others. Is this still valid if $P < m k - k + 1$?

negatives.text: Let $m \geq 3$ and $n \geq 2$ be integers. Prove that in a group of $N = m n - n + 1$ people such that there are no two familiar people among any $m$, there is a person who is unfamiliar with $n$ people. Does the statement remain true if $N < m n - n + 1$?

Let $m \geq 3$ and $n \geq 2$ be integers. Prove that in a group of $N = m n - n + 1$ people such that there are two familiar people among any $m$, there is a person who is familiar with at most $n$ people. Does the statement remain true if $N < m n - n + 1$?

Let $m \geq 3$ and $n \geq 2$ be integers. Prove that in a group of $N = m n - n + 1$ people such that there is at most one pair of familiar people among any $m$, there is a person who is familiar with $n$ people. Does the statement remain true if $N < m n - n + 1$?

positive_text: Let $ k $ be an integer, $ 1 < k < 100 $. For each arrangement $ b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots, b_{100} $ of the integers $ 1, 2, \ldots, 100 $, define $ b_{101} = 0 $ and find the smallest index $ n > k $ such that $ b_{n} $ is smaller than at least $ k - 1 $ of the values $ b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots, b_{k} $. Determine all $ k $ for which the total number of such arrangements with $ b_{n} = 1 $ equals $ \frac{100!}{4} $.

negatives.text: Let $ k $ be an integer, $ 1 < k < 100 $. For every permutation $ a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{100} $ of the integers $ 1, 2, \ldots, 100 $, set $ a_{101} = 0 $ and choose the least integer $ m > k $ such that $ a_{m} $ is greater than at least $ k - 1 $ of the numbers $ a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{k} $. Find all $ k $ for which the number of permutations with $ a_{m} = 1 $, is equal to $ \frac{100!}{4} $.

Let $ k $ be an integer, $ 1 < k < 100 $. For every permutation $ a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{100} $ of the integers $ 1, 2, \ldots, 100 $, set $ a_{101} = 0 $ and choose the least integer $ m > k $ such that $ a_{m} $ is less than at least $ k $ of the numbers $ a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{k} $. Find all $ k $ for which the number of permutations with $ a_{m} = 1 $, is equal to $ \frac{100!}{4} $.

Let $ k $ be an integer, $ 1 < k < 100 $. For every permutation $ a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{100} $ of the integers $ 1, 2, \ldots, 100 $, set $ a_{101} = 100 $ and choose the least integer $ m > k $ such that $ a_{m} $ is less than at least $ k - 1 $ of the numbers $ a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{k} $. Find all $ k $ for which the number of permutations with $ a_{m} = 1 $, is equal to $ \frac{100!}{4} $.

positive_text: Determine all real numbers $a$ for which the largest value attained by $f(x) = \frac{a x - 1}{x^{4} - x^{2} + 1}$ is exactly $1$.

negatives.text: Find all values of $a$ such that the maximum of the function $f(x) = \frac{a x + 1}{x^{4} - x^{2} + 1}$ is equal to $1$.
Find all values of $a$ such that the minimum of the function $f(x) = \frac{a x - 1}{x^{4} - x^{2} + 1}$ is equal to $1$.
Find all values of $a$ such that the maximum of the function $f(x) = \frac{a x - 1}{x^{4} + x^{2} + 1}$ is equal to $1$.

positive_text: Show that for each integer $k \geq 4$, there are infinitely many squarefree integers $m$ such that $k^m - 1$ is divisible by $m$.

negatives.text: Prove that for any integer $a \geq 4$ there exist infinitely many squarefree positive integers $n$ such that $a^n + 1$ is divisible by $n$.
Prove that for any integer $a \geq 4$ there exist infinitely many squarefree positive integers $n$ such that $a^{n} - 1$ is divisible by $n^2$.
Prove that for any integer $a \geq 4$ there exist infinitely many squarefree positive integers $n$ such that $n$ divides $a^{n-1} - 1$.

positive_text: Let $ABCD$ be a tangential quadrilateral. Determine $\angle BCD$ given that $BC = AC$, $AD = 5$, and the point $E = AC \cap BD$ satisfies $BE = 12$ and $DE = 3$.

negatives.text: Let $ABCD$ be a circumscribed quadrilateral. Find $\angle BCD$ if $AC = CD$, $AD = 5$, $E = AC \cap BD$, $BE = 12$ and $DE = 3$.
Let $ABCD$ be a circumscribed quadrilateral. Find $\angle BCD$ if $AC = BC$, $AD = 5$, $E = AC \cap BD$, $BE = 12$ and $DE = 5$.

positive_text:
a) Let $S$ be a subset of the positive integers less than $2000000$ containing $2000$ such that for all $x, y \in S$ with $x < y$, $x$ divides $y$. Determine the maximum size of $S$.

b) How many such subsets $S$ of maximum size exist?

negatives.text:
a) A set $A$ of positive integers less than $2000000$ is called good if $2000 \in A$ and $b$ divides $a$ for any $a, b \in A$, $a < b$. Find the maximum possible cardinality of a good set.

b) Find the number of the good sets of maximal cardinality.

a) A set $A$ of positive integers less than $2000000$ is called good if $2000 \in A$ and $a^2$ divides $b$ for any $a, b \in A$, $a < b$. Find the maximum possible cardinality of a good set.

b) Find the number of the good sets of maximal cardinality.

positive_text: Determine all non-constant polynomials $A(x)$ and $B(x)$ with real coefficients such that $A(x) B(x+1) = A(x+2004) B(x)$ for all $x$.

negatives.text: Find all non-constant polynomials $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ with real coefficients such that $P(x) Q(x+1) = P(x-2004) Q(x)$ for any $x$.
Find all non-constant polynomials $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ with real coefficients such that $P(x) Q(x+1)^2 = P(x+2004) Q(x)$ for any $x$.
Find all non-constant polynomials $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ with real coefficients such that $P(x) Q(x+2004) = P(x+1) Q(x)$ for any $x$.

positive_text: Let $S = \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$, $n \geq 4$. For any function $g: S \rightarrow S$ and any $x \in S$, define $g_1(x) = g(x)$, $g_{i+1}(x) = g(g_i(x))$, $i \geq 1$. Determine how many such functions $g$ satisfy the condition that $g_{n-2}$ is constant but $g_{n-3}$ is not.

negatives.text: Let $A = \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$, $n \geq 4$. For any function $f: A \rightarrow A$ and any $a \in A$, define $f_1(a) = f(a)$, $f_{i+1}(a) = f(f_i(a))$, $i \geq 1$. Find the number of the functions $f$ such that $f_{n-2}$ is not a constant function but $f_{n-3}$ is.

Let $A = \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$, $n \geq 4$. For any function $f: A \rightarrow A$ and any $a \in A$, define $f_1(a) = f(a)$, $f_{i+1}(a) = f(f_i(a))$, $i \geq 1$. Find the number of the functions $f$ such that $f_{n-2}$ is a constant function and $f_{n-3}$ is also constant.

Let $A = \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$, $n \geq 4$. For any function $f: A \rightarrow A$ and any $a \in A$, define $f_1(a) = f(a)$, $f_{i+1}(a) = f(f_i(a))$, $i \geq 1$. Find the number of the functions $f$ such that $f_{n-2}$ is a constant function and $f_{n-3}$ is injective.

positive_text: Suppose $A(x)$ and $B(x)$ are polynomials with at least two non-zero terms. If $\frac{A(x)}{B(x)}$ is not a constant, determine the minimal number of non-zero terms in the polynomial $F(s, t) = A(s) B(t) - A(t) B(s)$.

negatives.text: Let $p(x)$ and $q(x)$ be polynomials with $m \geq 2$ non-zero coefficients. If $\frac{p(x)}{q(x)}$ is not a constant function, find the least possible number of the non-zero coefficients of the polynomial $f(u, v) = p(u) q(v) + p(v) q(u)$.

Let $p(x)$ and $q(x)$ be polynomials with $m \geq 2$ non-zero coefficients. If $\frac{p(x)}{q(x)}$ is not a constant function, find the least possible number of the non-zero coefficients of the polynomial $f(u, v) = p(u) q(v) - p(v) q(u)^2$.

Let $p(x)$ and $q(x)$ be polynomials with $m \geq 2$ non-zero coefficients. If $\frac{p(x)}{q(x)}$ is not a constant function, find the least possible number of the non-zero coefficients of the polynomial $f(u, v) = p(u) q(v) - p(v) q(u)$, given that $p$ and $q$ are both monic.

positive_text: Let $P$ and $Q$ be points on the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ of a quadrilateral $ABCD$, such that $\frac{AP}{AC} + \frac{BQ}{BD} = 1$. Suppose the line $PQ$ intersects the sides $AD$ and $BC$ at points $M$ and $N$, respectively. Show that the circumcircles of triangles $AMP$, $BNQ$, $DMQ$, and $CNP$ have a common point.

negatives.text: Let $P$ and $Q$ be points on the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ of a quadrilateral $ABCD$ such that $\frac{AP}{AC} - \frac{BQ}{BD} = 1$. Suppose the line $PQ$ intersects the sides $AD$ and $BC$ at points $M$ and $N$. Prove that the circumcircles of triangles $AMP$, $BNQ$, $DMQ$, and $CNP$ are concurrent.

Let $P$ and $Q$ lie on the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ of a quadrilateral $ABCD$, such that $\frac{AP}{AC} + \frac{BQ}{BD} = 1$. The line $PQ$ intersects the sides $AB$ and $CD$ at points $M$ and $N$. Prove that the circumcircles of triangles $AMP$, $BNQ$, $DMQ$, and $CNP$ are concurrent.

Let $P$ and $Q$ lie on the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ of a quadrilateral $ABCD$ such that $\frac{AP}{AC} + \frac{BQ}{BD} = 1$. The line $PQ$ intersects the sides $AD$ and $BC$ at points $M$ and $N$. Prove that the circumcircles of triangles $AMP$, $BNQ$, $DMQ$, and $CNP$ are tangent to each other.

positive_text: Let $a$, $b$ and $m$ be positive integers. Define $K(m)$ as the number of ways to write $1$ as a sum of $m$ terms of the form $\frac{1}{k}$, where $k$ is a positive integer. Let $L(a, b)$ be the smallest positive integer $n$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{1}{x_{i}}=\frac{a}{b}$ has a solution in positive integers, and define $L(b)=\max \{L(a, b) \mid 1 \leq a \leq b\}$. Prove that the total number of positive divisors of $b$ is at most $2 L(b)+K(L(b)+2)$.

negatives.text: Let $a$, $b$ and $m$ be positive integers. Define $K(m)$ as the number of ways to write $1$ as a sum of $m$ terms of the form $\frac{1}{k^2}$, where $k$ is a positive integer. Let $L(a, b)$ be the smallest positive integer $n$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{1}{x_{i}}=\frac{a}{b}$ has a solution in positive integers, and define $L(b)=\max \{L(a, b) \mid 1 \leq a \leq b\}$. Prove that the total number of positive divisors of $b$ is at most $2 L(b)+K(L(b)+2)$.

Let $a$, $b$ and $m$ be positive integers. Define $K(m)$ as the number of ways to write $1$ as a sum of $m$ terms of the form $\frac{1}{k}$, where $k$ is a positive integer. Let $L(a, b)$ be the smallest positive integer $n$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{1}{x_{i}}=\frac{a}{b}$ has a solution in positive integers, and define $L(b)=\max \{L(a, b) \mid 1 \leq a \leq b\}$. Prove that the total number of positive divisors of $b$ is at most $2 L(b)+K(L(b)-2)$.

positive_text: Let $G$ be a graph with $2n$ vertices, where $n \geq 4$. Each edge is colored either red or blue. It is given that the graph has no blue triangle and no red clique of size $n$. Determine the minimum number of blue edges in $G$.

negatives.text: The edges of a graph with $2n$ vertices, $n \geq 4$, are colored in blue and red such that there is no blue triangle and there is no red complete subgraph with $n+1$ vertices. Find the least possible number of the blue edges.

The edges of a graph with $2n$ vertices, $n \geq 4$, are colored in blue and red such that there is no blue triangle and there is no red complete subgraph with $n$ vertices. Find the least possible number of the red edges.

The edges of a graph with $2n$ vertices, $n \geq 4$, are colored in blue and red such that there is no red triangle and there is no blue complete subgraph with $n$ vertices. Find the least possible number of the blue edges.

positive_text: Let the internal angle bisectors of $\triangle ABC$ intersect the circumcircle at $A_1$, $B_1$, and $C_1$. Let $I = AA_1 \cap CC_1$, $N = AA_1 \cap BC$, and $P = BB_1 \cap A_1C_1$. Let $O$ be the circumcenter of $\triangle IPC_1$, and let $M = OP \cap BC$. If $BM = MN$ and $\angle BAC = 2\angle ABC$, determine the angles of triangle $ABC$.

negatives.text: Let the internal angle bisectors of $\triangle ABC$ intersect the circumcircle at $A_1$, $B_1$, and $C_1$. Let $I = AA_1 \cap CC_1$, $N = AA_1 \cap BC$, and $P = BB_1 \cap A_1C_1$. Let $O$ be the circumcenter of $\triangle IPC_1$, and let $M = OP \cap BC$. If $BM = 2MN$ and $\angle BAC = 2\angle ABC$, determine the angles of triangle $ABC$.

Let the internal angle bisectors of $\triangle ABC$ intersect the circumcircle at $A_1$, $B_1$, and $C_1$. Let $I = AA_1 \cap CC_1$, $N = AA_1 \cap BC$, and $P = BB_1 \cap A_1C_1$. Let $O$ be the circumcenter of $\triangle IPC_1$, and let $M = OP \cap BC$. If $BM = MN$ and $\angle BAC = 2\angle ACB$, determine the angles of triangle $ABC$.

positive_text:
Determine all values of $a$ for which the quadratic equation
$$
(a^{2}-a-9) x^{2}-6 x-a=0
$$
has two real, positive, and distinct solutions.

negatives.text:
Find all values of $a$ such that the equation
$$
(a^{2}-a-9) x^{2}+6 x-a=0
$$
has two distinct positive roots.

Find all values of $a$ such that the equation
$$
(a^{2}-a-9) x^{2}-6 x-a=0
$$
has two distinct negative roots.

Find all values of $a$ such that the equation
$$
(a^{2}-a-9) x^{2}-6 x-a=0
$$
has two equal positive roots.

positive_text:
Determine all values of $a$ for which the equation
$$
\sqrt{(4a^2 - 4a - 1)x^2 - 2a x + 1} = 1 - x(ax + 1)
$$
has exactly two real solutions.

negatives.text:
Find all values of $a$ such that the equation
$$
\sqrt{(4a^2 - 4a - 1)x^2 - 2a x + 1} = 1 + ax - x^2
$$
has exactly two solutions.

Find all values of $a$ such that the equation
$$
\sqrt{(4a^2 - 4a - 1)x^2 - 2a x + 1} = 1 - a x^2 - x
$$
has exactly two solutions.

Find all values of $a$ such that the equation
$$
\sqrt{(4a^2 - 4a - 1)x^2 - 2a x + 1} = 1 - ax - x^2
$$
has exactly one solution.

positive_text: \begin{cases} x^{2} + y^{2} = a^{2} + 2 \\ \dfrac{x + y}{xy} = a \end{cases} where $a$ is a real number.\text{ a) Solve the system for $a=0$.\text{ b) Find all $a$, for which the system has exactly two solutions.

negatives.text: \begin{cases} x^{2} + y^{2} = a^{2} + 2 \\ \dfrac{1}{x} - \dfrac{1}{y} = a \end{cases} where $a$ is a real number.\text{ a) Solve the system for $a=0$.\text{ b) Find all $a$, for which the system has exactly two solutions.

\begin{cases} x^{2} + y^{2} = a^{2} + 2 \\ \dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{1}{y} = a \\ x + y = 1 \end{cases} where $a$ is a real number.\text{ a) Solve the system for $a=0$.\text{ b) Find all $a$, for which the system has exactly two solutions.

\begin{cases} x^{2} + y^{2} = a^{2} + 2 \\ \dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{1}{y} = a^{2} \end{cases} where $a$ is a real number.\text{ a) Solve the system for $a=0$.\text{ b) Find all $a$, for which the system has exactly two solutions.

positive_text: Suppose $I$ is the incenter of triangle $ABC$ and $M$ is the midpoint of segment $AB$. Determine the smallest possible measure of angle $\angle CIM$ under the condition that $CI = MI$.

negatives.text: Let $I$ be the incenter of $\triangle ABC$ and $M$ be the midpoint of side $AB$. Find the least possible value of $\Varangle CIM$ if $CI < MI$.

positive_text: Let $P$ and $Q$ lie on segments $AC$ and $BC$ of isosceles triangle $\triangle ABC$ (where $AC = BC$) such that $4 AP \cdot BQ = AB^2$. Prove that line $AB$ and the angle bisectors of $\angle APQ$ and $\angle BQP$ are concurrent.

negatives.text: Let $A_1$ and $B_1$ be points on the sides $AC$ and $BC$ of $\triangle ABC$ such that $4 AA_1 \cdot BB_1 = AB^2$. If $AC = 2BC$, prove that the line $AB$ and the bisectors of $\angle AA_1B_1$ and $\angle BB_1A_1$ are concurrent.

positive_text: In a cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ with circumcenter $O$, let the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $F$. Suppose the midpoints of $AD$, $BC$, and $OF$ lie on a straight line. Show that $AB = CD$.

negatives.text: The diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ of a cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ with circumcenter $I$ intersect at a point $E$. If the midpoints of segments $AB$, $CD$, and $IE$ are collinear, prove that $AB = CD$.

The diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ of a cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ with circumcenter $I$ intersect at a point $E$. If the midpoints of segments $AD$, $BC$, and $IE$ are collinear, prove that $AB + CD = BC + AD$.

positive_text: Let $x, y, z > 0$ with $x + y + z = 1$. Show that $$\frac{9}{10} \leq \frac{x}{1 + yz} + \frac{y}{1 + zx} + \frac{z}{1 + xy} < 1$$

negatives.text: Let $a, b, c > 0$ and $a + b + c = 1$. Prove that $$\frac{a}{1 - bc} + \frac{b}{1 - ca} + \frac{c}{1 - ab} < 1$$
Let $a, b, c > 0$ and $a + b + c = 1$. Prove that $$\frac{a^2}{1 + bc} + \frac{b^2}{1 + ca} + \frac{c^2}{1 + ab} < 1$$
Let $a, b, c > 0$ and $a + b + c = 1$. Prove that $$\frac{a}{1 + b^2 c^2} + \frac{b}{1 + c^2 a^2} + \frac{c}{1 + a^2 b^2} < 1$$

positive_text: \text{Find all integer solutions to} \quad x^{3}+10x-1=y^{3}+6y^{2}

negatives.text: \text{Solve in integers } x, y \text{ such that } x^{3}+10x+1=y^{3}+6y^{2}
\text{Solve in integers } x, y \text{ such that } x^{3}+10x-1=y^{3}-6y^{2}
\text{Solve in integers } x, y \text{ such that } x^{3}+10x-1=y^{3}+6y^{2}+y

positive_text: Given an $n \times n$ square grid ($n \geq 2$), each cell is colored black or white. For any rectangle (with at least four cells), the four corner cells are not all of the same color. Determine the largest possible value of $n$.

negatives.text: A square $n \times n$ ($n \geq 2$) is divided into $n^{2}$ unit squares colored in black or white such that the squares at the four corners of any rectangle (containing at least four squares) have the same color. Find the maximum possible value of $n$.

A square $n \times n$ ($n \geq 2$) is divided into $n^{2}$ unit squares colored in black or white such that the squares at the four corners of any square (containing at least four squares) have not the same color. Find the maximum possible value of $n$.

positive_text:
Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle. Determine the set of all points $M$ inside $\triangle ABC$ for which the following equation holds:
$$
AB - FG = \frac{MF \cdot AG + MG \cdot BF}{CM}
$$
where $F$ and $G$ denote the projections of $M$ onto $BC$ and $AC$, respectively.

negatives.text:
Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle. Find the locus of the points $M$ in the interior of $\triangle ABC$ such that
$$
AB + FG = \frac{MF \cdot AG + MG \cdot BF}{CM}
$$
where $F$ and $G$ are the feet of the perpendiculars from $M$ to the lines $BC$ and $AC$, respectively.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle. Find the locus of the points $M$ in the interior of $\triangle ABC$ such that
$$
AB - FG = \frac{MF \cdot AG - MG \cdot BF}{CM}
$$
where $F$ and $G$ are the feet of the perpendiculars from $M$ to the lines $BC$ and $AC$, respectively.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle. Find the locus of the points $M$ in the interior of $\triangle ABC$ such that
$$
AB - FG = \frac{MF \cdot AG + MG \cdot BF}{MC^2}
$$
where $F$ and $G$ are the feet of the perpendiculars from $M$ to the lines $BC$ and $AC$, respectively.

positive_text:
Let $f(x) = |x^{2} - 5x + 6|$ and consider the inequality $f(x) \leq x + a$ with $a \in \mathbb{R}$.

a) Determine the solution set when $a = 0$.

b) Find the real values of $a$ such that the inequality has exactly three integer solutions.

negatives.text:
Consider the inequality $|x^{2} - 5x + 6| < x + a$, where $a$ is a real parameter.

a) Solve the inequality for $a = 0$.

b) Find the values of $a$ for which the inequality has exactly three integer solutions.

Consider the inequality $|x^{2} + 5x + 6| \leq x + a$, where $a$ is a real parameter.

a) Solve the inequality for $a = 0$.

b) Find the values of $a$ for which the inequality has exactly three integer solutions.

Consider the inequality $|x^{2} - 5x + 6| \leq -x + a$, where $a$ is a real parameter.

a) Solve the inequality for $a = 0$.

b) Find the values of $a$ for which the inequality has exactly three integer solutions.

positive_text: \text{Find all real numbers } x \text{ such that } (x+6) 5^{1-|x-1|} - x = (x+1)\left|5^{x}-1\right| + 5^{x+1} + 1.

negatives.text: \text{Solve the equation } (x+6) 5^{1-|x-1|} + x = (x+1)\left|5^{x}-1\right| + 5^{x+1} + 1.
\text{Solve the equation } (x+6) 5^{1-|x-1|} - x = (x+1)\left|5^{x}-1\right| + 5^{x-1} + 1.
\text{Solve the equation } (x+6) 5^{1-|x-1|} - x = (x+1)\left|5^{-x}-1\right| + 5^{x+1} + 1.

positive_text:
Find all integer solutions to the equation
$$
 a^{2}+1 = bc(bc + 2c - 2b - 4).
$$

negatives.text:
Solve in integers the equation
$$
 z^{2} - 1 = xy(xy + 2y - 2x - 4).
$$

Solve in integers the equation
$$
 z^{2} + 1 = xy(xy + 2y + 2x - 4).
$$

Solve in integers the equation
$$

$$

positive_text: Let $A$ be an $n \times n$ grid with $n \geq 2$, where each cell is filled with either $1$ or $-1$. Let the neighbors of a cell $(i, j)$ be defined as the cells $(i, (j \pm 1) \mod n)$ and $((i \pm 1) \mod n, j)$. In one move, each cell $(i, j)$ is updated to the product of the values in its four neighbors. A grid is said to be "stable" if it can be transformed into the all-ones grid through a finite sequence of such moves. Determine all values of $n$ for which every such $n \times n$ grid is stable.

negatives.text: In every cell of a table $n \times n$, $n \geq 2$, one of the numbers $+1$ and $-1$ is written. The neighbors of the cell $(i, j)$ are the cells $(i, j-1)$, $(i, j+1)$, $(i-1, j)$ and $(i+1, j)$, where the numbers are taken modulo $n$. At each step one replaces the number in each cell with the sum of the numbers in the four neighbors of that cell. A table is called "good" if after finitely many steps one obtains the table with $+1$ in every cell. Find all values of $n$ such that every table $n \times n$ is "good".

In every cell of a table $n \times n$, $n \geq 2$, one of the numbers $+1$ and $-1$ is written. The neighbors of the cell $(i, j)$ are the cells $(i, j-1)$, $(i, j+1)$, $(i-1, j)$ and $(i+1, j)$, where the numbers are taken modulo $n$. At each step one replaces the number in each cell with the product of the numbers in the four neighbors of that cell, but only if that product is $-1$; otherwise, the value remains unchanged. A table is called "good" if after finitely many steps one obtains the table with $+1$ in every cell. Find all values of $n$ such that every table $n \times n$ is "good".

In every cell of a table $n \times n$, $n \geq 2$, one of the numbers $+1$ and $-1$ is written. The neighbors of the cell $(i, j)$ are the cells $(i, j-1)$, $(i, j+1)$, $(i-1, j)$ and $(i+1, j)$, where the numbers are taken modulo $n$. At each step one replaces the number in each cell with the product of the numbers in the three neighbors of that cell (excluding the cell directly below it). A table is called "good" if after finitely many steps one obtains the table with $+1$ in every cell. Find all values of $n$ such that every table $n \times n$ is "good".

positive_text:
Determine all real values of the parameter $a$ for which the number of solutions to the equation
$$
15 x^{2} - 2 x - 3 a^{4} = 12 a^{2} x - 2 a^{2}
$$
is less than or equal to the number of solutions to the equation
$$
2 x^{3} + 6 x = \left(3^{6 a}-9\right) \sqrt{2^{8 a}-\frac{1}{6}} - (3 a - 1)^{2} 12^{x}
$$
