positive_text: Sei $\sigma = (b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots, b_{n})$ eine Permutation der Zahlen $1,2, \ldots, n$. Die Anzahl der Inversionen von $\sigma$ ist definiert als die Anzahl Paare $(i, j)$ mit $1 \leq i<j \leq n$ und $b_{j} > b_{i}$. Zeige, dass für jede ganze Zahl $m$ mit $0 \leq m \leq\binom{n}{2}$, es eine Permutation der Zahlen $1,2, \ldots, n$ gibt, die genau $m$ Inversionen hat.

negatives.text: Sei $\pi = (a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n})$ eine Permutation der Zahlen $1,2, \ldots, n$. Die Verwuselung von $\pi$ ist die Anzahl Paare $(i, j)$ mit $1 \leq i<j \leq n$ und $a_{j} < a_{i}$. Beweise, dass es für jede ganze Zahl $k$ mit $0 \leq k \leq\binom{n}{2}$ eine Permutation der Zahlen $1,2, \ldots, n$ mit Verwuselung $k$ gibt.

Sei $\pi = (a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n})$ eine Permutation der Zahlen $1,2, \ldots, n$. Die Verwuselung von $\pi$ ist die Anzahl Paare $(i, j)$ mit $1 \leq i \neq j \leq n$ und $a_{j} > a_{i}$. Beweise, dass es für jede ganze Zahl $k$ mit $0 \leq k \leq\binom{n}{2}$ eine Permutation der Zahlen $1,2, \ldots, n$ mit Verwuselung $k$ gibt.

Beweise, dass es für jede ganze Zahl $k$ mit $0 \leq k \leq\binom{n}{2}$ eine Permutation der Zahlen $1,2, \ldots, n$ mit Verwuselung $k$ gibt.

Beweise die Ungleichung $\ell(P) < |P| + 2$ und zeige, dass Gleichheit gilt, wenn das kleinste Element von $P$ kleiner als $|P|$ ist.

positive_text: Soit $n$ un entier strictement positif. Maurice considère l'ensemble $\{1,2, \ldots, n\}$, et pour chaque sous-ensemble non-vide, il calcule le produit de ses éléments. Il additionne ensuite les inverses de tous ces produits. Exprimer, en fonction de $n$, la valeur obtenue.

negatives.text: Soit $n$ un entier strictement positif. Maurice écrit tous les $2^{n}-1$ sous-ensembles non-vides de $\{1,2, \ldots, n\}$, et pour chacun, il écrit la somme de ses éléments. Il additionne ensuite les inverses de ces valeurs. Quelle est la somme obtenue en fonction de $n$?

positive_text:
Let $G$ be a simple graph with $n \geq 2$ vertices $v_{1}, v_{2}, \ldots, v_{n}$ and $m \geq 1$ edges. Two players, Joël and Robert, play a game with $m$ coins as follows:

i) Joël assigns a non-negative integer $w_{i}$ to each vertex $v_{i}$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^{n} w_{i} = m$.

ii) Robert selects a subset of edges (possibly empty) and, for each selected edge, places one coin on either of its two endpoints. After this step, the number of coins on any vertex $v_{i}$ must be $\leq w_{i}$.

iii) Joël then performs the same action on the remaining edges.

iv) Joël wins if the final number of coins on each vertex $v_{i}$ equals $w_{i}$.

Characterize all graphs $G$ for which Joël can guarantee a win.

negatives.text:
Let $G$ be a simple graph with $n \geq 2$ vertices $v_{1}, v_{2}, \ldots, v_{n}$ and $m \geq 1$ edges. Joël and Robert play a game with $m$ coins as follows:

i) Joël assigns a non-negative integer $w_{i}$ to each vertex $v_{i}$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^{n} w_{i} = m$.

ii) Robert selects a subset of edges (possibly empty) and places a coin on exactly one of its endpoints, then removes the edge from the graph. When he is done, the amount of coins on each vertex $v_{i}$ should be strictly less than $w_{i}$.

iii) Joël then does the same for all the remaining edges.

iv) Joël wins if the number of coins on each vertex $v_{i}$ is equal to $w_{i}$.

Determine all such graphs $G$ for which Joël has a winning strategy.

Let $G$ be a simple graph with $n \geq 2$ vertices $v_{1}, v_{2}, \ldots, v_{n}$ and $m \geq 1$ edges. Joël and Robert play a game with $m$ coins as follows:

i) Joël assigns a non-negative integer $w_{i}$ to each vertex $v_{i}$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^{n} w_{i} = m$.

ii) Robert selects a subset of edges (possibly empty) and places a coin on exactly one of its endpoints, then removes the edge from the graph. When he is done, the amount of coins on each vertex $v_{i}$ should not be greater than $w_{i}$.

iii) Joël then does the same for all the remaining edges.

iv) Joël wins if the number of coins on each vertex $v_{i}$ is at least $w_{i}$.

Determine all such graphs $G$ for which Joël has a winning strategy.

positive_text:
Let $k \geq 2$ be an integer. Prove that if
$$
\frac{k^{2}+4^{k}+7^{k}}{k}
$$
is an integer, then it is divisible by $11$.

negatives.text:
Let $n \geq 2$ be an integer. Prove that if
$$
\frac{n^{2} - 4^{n} + 7^{n}}{n}
$$
is an integer, then it is divisible by $11$.

Let $n \geq 2$ be an integer. Prove that if
$$
\frac{n^{2}+4^{n}+7^{n}+1}{n}
$$
is an integer, then it is divisible by $11$.

Let $n \geq 2$ be an integer. Prove that if
$$
\frac{n^{2}+4^{n}+7^{n}}{n+1}
$$
is an integer, then it is divisible by $11$.

positive_text: Let $n \geq 3$ be an integer. Suppose there are infinitely many tokens in each of $n$ distinct hues. Given an integer $m \geq n+1$ and a circular arrangement of $m$ individuals, assign one token to each such that every set of $n+1$ adjacent individuals has tokens of all $n$ hues. Prove that only finitely many values of $m$ make this impossible and find the maximum such $m$ in terms of $n$.

negatives.text: Let $n \geq 3$ be an integer. Annalena has infinitely many cowbells in each of $n$ different colours. Given an integer $m \geq n+1$ and a group of $m$ cows standing in a circle, she is tasked with tying one cowbell around the neck of every cow so that every group of $n+1$ consecutive cows have cowbells of at least one repeated colour. Prove that there are only finitely many values of $m$ for which this is not possible and determine the largest such $m$ in terms of $n$.

Let $n \geq 3$ be an integer. Annalena has infinitely many cowbells in each of $n$ different colours. Given an integer $m \geq n+1$ and a group of $m$ cows standing in a line (not a circle), she is tasked with tying one cowbell around the neck of every cow so that every group of $n+1$ consecutive cows have cowbells of all the possible $n$ colours. Prove that there are only finitely many values of $m$ for which this is not possible and determine the largest such $m$ in terms of $n$.

Let $n \geq 3$ be an integer. Annalena has infinitely many cowbells in each of $n$ different colours. Given an integer $m \geq n+1$ and a group of $m$ cows standing in a circle, she is tasked with tying one cowbell around the neck of every cow so that every group of $n$ consecutive cows have cowbells of all the possible $n$ colours. Prove that there are only finitely many values of $m$ for which this is not possible and determine the largest such $m$ in terms of $n$.

positive_text:
Let $k$ be a positive integer. Determine all polynomials $Q$ with real coefficients such that
$$
Q\left(x^{2}+x-k^{2}\right)=Q(x)^{2}+Q(x)
$$
holds for all real values of $x$.

negatives.text:
Let $n$ be a positive integer. Find all polynomials $P$ with real coefficients such that
$$
P\left(x^{2}+x+n^{2}\right)=P(x)^{2}+P(x)
$$
for all real numbers $x$.

Let $n$ be a positive integer. Find all polynomials $P$ with real coefficients such that
$$
P\left(x^{2}+x-n^{2}\right)=P(x)^{2}-P(x)
$$
for all real numbers $x$.

Let $n$ be a positive integer. Find all polynomials $P$ with real coefficients such that
$$
\left(P\left(x^{2}+x-n^{2}\right)\right)^{2}=P(x)^{2}+P(x)
$$
for all real numbers $x$.

positive_text:
Let $n \geq 2$ be an integer, and suppose we have all subsets of a set of $n$ elements (excluding the empty set). These subsets are assigned to rooms such that no element appears in more than one subset per room.

a. Prove that it is possible to assign them to $2^{n-1}$ rooms.

b. Prove that it is impossible to assign them to fewer than $2^{n-1}$ rooms.

negatives.text:
A class of $n \geq 2$ children takes group pictures for every non-empty subset. These pictures are hung in rooms such that no child appears in more than one photo per room.

a. Show that this is possible if the school has $2^{n-2}$ rooms.

b. Show that this is not possible if the school has more than $2^{n-1}$ rooms.

A class of $n \geq 2$ children takes group pictures for every non-empty subset. These pictures are hung in rooms such that no child appears in more than one photo per room.

a. Show that this is possible if the school has $2^{n-1} - 1$ rooms.

b. Show that this is not possible if the school has less than $2^{n-1} - 1$ rooms.

A class of $n \geq 2$ children takes group pictures for every non-empty subset. These pictures are hung in rooms such that no child appears in more than one photo per room.

a. Show that this is possible if the school has $2^{n-1}$ rooms.

b. Show that this is not possible if the school has fewer than $2^{n-1} + 1$ rooms.

positive_text:
Find all pairs $(a, q)$ with $a$ a positive integer and $q$ a prime number such that
$$
q^{2} + q a = a^{3}.
$$

negatives.text:
Find all pairs $(m, p)$ with $m$ a positive integer and $p$ a prime number such that
$$
p^{2} - p m = m^{3}.
$$

Determine all pairs $(m, p)$ with $m$ a positive integer and $p$ a prime number satisfying the equation
$$
p^{3} + p m = m^{3}.
$$

Determine all pairs $(m, p)$ with $m$ a positive integer and $p$ a prime number satisfying the inequality
$$
p^{2} + p m < m^{3}.
$$

positive_text: Let $p$ be any prime number and let $b_{0}, b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots$ be integers defined by $b_{0} = b_{1} = 0$ and $$ b_{n+2} = c \cdot b_{n+1} + d \cdot b_{n} + 1 $$ for all $n \geq 0$. Prove that $\gcd(b_{p}, b_{p+1})$ is either $1$ or greater than $\sqrt{p}$.

negatives.text: Let $x$, $y$ and $a_{0}$, $a_{1}$, $a_{2}$, $\ldots$ be integers satisfying $a_{0}=a_{1}=0$ and $$ a_{n+2}=x \cdot a_{n+1}+y \cdot a_{n} - 1 $$ for all $n \geq 0$. Let $p$ be any prime number. Show that $\gcd(a_{p}, a_{p+1})$ is either $1$ or greater than $\sqrt{p}$.

Let $x$, $y$ and $a_{0}$, $a_{1}$, $a_{2}$, $\ldots$ be integers satisfying $a_{0}=a_{1}=0$ and $$ a_{n+2}=x \cdot a_{n+1} + y \cdot a_{n} + 1 $$ for all $n \geq 0$. Let $p$ be any prime number. Show that $\gcd(a_{p}, a_{p-1})$ is either $1$ or greater than $\sqrt{p}$.

Let $x$, $y$ and $a_{0}$, $a_{1}$, $a_{2}$, $\ldots$ be integers satisfying $a_{0}=a_{1}=0$ and $$ a_{n+2}=x \cdot a_{n+1} + y \cdot a_{n} + 1 $$ for all $n \geq 0$. Let $p$ be any prime number. Show that $\gcd(a_{p^2}, a_{p+1})$ is either $1$ or greater than $\sqrt{p}$.

positive_text: Suppose $ABC$ and $AMN$ are similar, non-overlapping triangles with the same orientation, and $AB = AC$, $AM = AN$. If $O$ is the circumcenter of triangle $MAB$, show that $A$, $C$, $N$, and $O$ are concyclic if and only if triangle $ABC$ is equilateral.

negatives.text: Let $ABC$ and $AMN$ be two similar, non-overlapping triangles with the same orientation, such that $AB = AC$ and $AM = AN$. Let $O$ be the circumcenter of triangle $MAB$. Prove that the points $O$, $C$, $N$ and $B$ lie on a circle if and only if the triangle $ABC$ is equilateral.

Let $ABC$ and $AMN$ be two similar, non-overlapping triangles with the same orientation, such that $AB = AC$ and $AM = AN$. Let $O$ be the circumcenter of triangle $MAB$. Prove that the points $O$, $C$, $N$ and $A$ lie on a circle if and only if the triangle $ABC$ is isosceles.

Let $ABC$ and $AMN$ be two similar, non-overlapping triangles with the same orientation, such that $AB = AC$ and $AM = AN$. Let $O$ be the circumcenter of triangle $MAB$. Prove that the points $O$, $C$, $N$ and $A$ lie on a line if and only if the triangle $ABC$ is equilateral.

positive_text:
Find the minimum value of the expression
$$
\frac{x y+1}{x+y}+\frac{y z+1}{y+z}+\frac{z x+1}{z+x}
$$
where $x, y, z \in \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $x+y+z=-1$ and $x y z \leq -3$.

negatives.text:
Determine the smallest possible value of the expression
$$
\frac{a b+1}{a+b}+\frac{b c+1}{b+c}+\frac{c a+1}{c+a}
$$
where $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $a+b+c=1$ and $a b c \leq -3$.

positive_text: Find all monic polynomials $P(x) = x^{2023} + b_{2022} x^{2022} + \cdots + b_1 x + b_0$ with real coefficients such that $b_{2022} = 0$, $P(1) = 1$, and all real roots of $P$ are strictly less than $1$.

negatives.text: Determine all monic polynomials $P(x) = x^{2023} + a_{2022} x^{2022} + \cdots + a_0$ with real coefficients such that $a_{2022} = 0$, $P(1) = 1$, and all roots of $P$ are real and greater than $1$.
Find all monic polynomials $P(x) = x^{2023} + a_{2022} x^{2022} + \cdots + a_0$ with real coefficients such that $a_{2022} = 0$, $P(1) = -1$, and all roots of $P$ are real and less than $1$.

Determine all monic polynomials $P(x) = x^{2023} + a_{2022} x^{2022} + \cdots + a_0$ with real coefficients such that $a_{2022} = 0$, $P(1) = 1$, and all roots of $P$ are real and less than or equal to $1$.

positive_text: 已知 $x, y, z, w$ 為非負實數, 試求滿足下列方程組的解 $(x, y, z, w)$: $$ x^2(y+z)(y+z+w) = \sqrt{y+z}\sqrt[3]{y+z+w} $$ $$ y^2(z+w)(z+w+x) = \sqrt{z+w}\sqrt[3]{z+w+x} $$ $$ z^2(w+x)(w+x+y) = \sqrt{w+x}\sqrt[3]{w+x+y} $$ $$ w^2(x+y)(x+y+z) = \sqrt{x+y}\sqrt[3]{x+y+z} $$

positive_text:

$$

f(x) - (f(y))^2 = k f(x + y^2).
$$

positive_text: 設 $G$ 與 $H$ 為頂點數相同 $n \ge 4$ 的圖，頂點編號為 $1, 2, \dots, n$。若對於任意 $1 \le i < j \le n$, 圖 $G$ 去掉頂點 $i$ 與 $j$ 後所得的圖與圖 $H$ 去掉頂點 $i$ 與 $j$ 後所得的圖同構，試證 $G$ 與 $H$ 是同構的。

positive_text:
令 $T$ 是 $[0, 1]$ 區間中所有有理數的集合。考慮一個無限實數數列
$$
\{a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n, \dots\},
$$
若存在一個由 $T$ 映至實數的函數 $G(x)$ 滿足：
(i) $G$ 在 $[0, \frac{1}{2}]$ 上為非遞減。即: 對任意 $0 \le a \le b \le \frac{1}{2}$, $G(a) \le G(b)$。
(ii) 對任意整數 $0 < m, 0 \le n \le m$, 都有
$$
G\left(\frac{n}{m}\right) = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_{m+1-i} - \sum_{i=1}^{n} a_i}{m}
$$
則稱此數列為「超乎想像」。求所有這樣的數列。

negatives.text:
令 $S$ 是 $[0, 1]$ 區間中所有有理數的集合。考慮一個無限實數數列
$$
\{x_1, x_2, \dots, x_k, \dots\},
$$
若存在一個由 $S$ 映至實數的函數 $H(x)$ 滿足：
(i) $H$ 在 $[0, \frac{1}{2}]$ 遞增。
(ii) 對任意整數 $0 < p, 0 \le q \le p$, 都有
$$
H\left(\frac{q}{p}\right) = \frac{\sum_{k=1}^{q} x_{p+1-k} + \sum_{k=1}^{q} x_k}{p}
$$
則稱此數列為「超乎想像」。求所有這樣的數列。

令 $S$ 是 $[0, 1]$ 區間中所有有理數的集合。考慮一個無限實數數列
$$
\{x_1, x_2, \dots, x_k, \dots\},
$$
若存在一個由 $S$ 映至實數的函數 $H(x)$ 滿足：
(i) $H$ 在 $[0, \frac{1}{2}]$ 遞增。
(ii) 對任意整數 $0 < p, 0 \le q \le p$, 都有
$$
H\left(\frac{q}{p}\right) = \frac{\sum_{k=1}^{q} x_{p+1-k} - \sum_{k=1}^{q} x_k}{2p}
$$
則稱此數列為「超乎想像」。求所有這樣的數列。

令 $S$ 是 $[0, 1]$ 區間中所有有理數的集合。考慮一個無限實數數列
$$
\{x_1, x_2, \dots, x_k, \dots\},
$$

H\left(\frac{q}{p}\right) = \frac{\sum_{k=1}^{q} x_{p+1-k} - \sum_{k=1}^{q} x_k}{p^2}
$$
則稱此數列為「超乎想像」。求所有這樣的數列。

positive_text:

positive_text: Let $k \ge 2$ be an integer. Two players, Alice and Bob, play a game with the following rules: A number $n \ge k$ is written on the board. Players alternate moves, starting with Alice, by replacing the number $m$ with a number $m'$ such that $k \le m' < m$ and $\gcd(m, m') = 1$. The player who cannot make a move loses. A number $n$ is called good if Bob has a winning strategy starting from $n$, and bad otherwise. If $n$ and $n'$ share the same set of prime divisors less than or equal to $k$, show that $n$ is good if and only if $n'$ is good.

negatives.text: Fix an integer $k \ge 2$. Two players, Ana and Banana, play the following game of numbers: Initially, some integer $n \ge k$ gets written on the blackboard. A number $n$ is good if Banana has a winning strategy from $n$. If $n$ and $n'$ share the same set of prime divisors less than or equal to $k$, prove that $n$ is good if and only if $n'$ is good.

positive_text:
令 $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n$ 為正整數且 $x_1 < x_2 < \dots < x_n$，$m$ 為正實數且 $m \ge 1$。
證明：
$$
\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i^{2m+1} \ge \left( \sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i^m \right)^2 .
$$

negatives.text:
令 $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ 為正整數且 $a_1 < a_2 < \dots < a_n$，$k$ 為正實數且 $k \ge 1$。
證明：
$$
\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_i^{2k-1} \ge \left( \sum_{i=1}^{n} a_i^k \right)^2 .
$$

令 $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ 為正整數且 $a_1 < a_2 < \dots < a_n$，$k$ 為正實數且 $k \ge 1$。

$$

positive_text:
令 $x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots$ 是整數數列且 $y_0, y_1, y_2, \dots$ 是正整數數列使得 $x_0 = 0, x_1 = 1$, 以及對於所有的 $n = 1, 2, \dots$, 都有
$$
x_{n+1} = \begin{cases} x_n y_n + x_{n-1} & \text{若 } y_{n-1} = 1; \\
 x_n y_n - x_{n-1} & \text{若 } y_{n-1} > 1. \end{cases}
$$
試證: 在 $x_{2017}$ 與 $x_{2018}$ 兩個數中至少有一個數大於或等於 2017.

positive_text:
令 $a, b$ 為不相等的正實數，且 $m$ 為大於 1 的整數。若
$$
  a^m - b^m = a^{m+1} - b^{m+1},
$$
試證:
$$
  1 < a + b < \frac{2m}{m + 1}.
$$

negatives.text:
設 $x, y$ 為相異正數, 且 $n$ 為大於 1 的正整數。若
$$
  x^n + y^n = x^{n+1} + y^{n+1},
$$
證明:
$$
  1 < x + y < \frac{2n}{n + 1}.
$$

設 $x, y$ 為相異正數, 且 $n$ 為大於 1 的正整數。若

$$

$$
  1 < x + y < \frac{2n}{n + 1}.
$$

positive_text: Let $ X $ be a finite set and let $ \Phi $ be the set of all mappings from $ X $ to $ X $. Let $ h \in \Phi $ and define $ Y = h(X) $ as the range of $ X $ under $ h $. Assume that for any $ k \in \Phi $ such that $ k \neq h $, it holds that $ h \circ k \circ h \neq k \circ h \circ k $. Prove that $ h(Y) = Y $.

設 $n$ 為大於 3 的正整數。房間中有 $n$ 個人，其中有些人之間存在敵對關係（敵對關係是雙向的）。假設我們知道這群人同時滿足以下兩個性質：

a. 任意 4 個人中，至少有 2 人之間沒有敵對關係。

b. 對於任何正整數 $m \ge 1$，若存在 $m$ 個人彼此之間沒有敵對關係，則在剩下的 $n - m$ 個人中，存在 3 個人，他們彼此之間都有敵對關係。

試求 $n$ 的最小可能值。

positive_text:
Is there a positive integer $ m $ such that the equation
$$
(a^3 - a)(b^3 - b) = mc^2
$$
has infinitely many positive integer triples $ (a, b, c) $ with $ a $ and $ b $ distinct?

negatives.text:
Does there exist a positive integer $ m $ for which the equation
$$
(a^3 + a)(b^3 + b) = mc^2
$$
has infinitely many positive integer solutions $ (a, b, c) $ in which $ a \neq b $?

Does there exist a positive integer $ m $ for which the equation
$$
(a^3 - a)(b^3 - b) = mc^3
$$
has infinitely many positive integer solutions $ (a, b, c) $ in which $ a \neq b $?

Does there exist a positive integer $ m $ for which the equation
$$
(a^3 - a)(b^3 - b) = mc^2
$$
has infinitely many positive integer solutions $ (a, b, c) $ in which $ a = b $?

f(ab + af(a)) = f(a)(f(a) + f(b)).
$$

positive_text: Let $S$ be a set of $n \ge 3$ positive integers such that the sum of any two distinct elements in $S$ is not in $S$. Prove that there exists an ordering $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n$ of the elements of $S$ such that for all $i = 2, 3, \dots, n-1$, $b_{i-1} + b_{i+1}$ and $b_{i-1} - b_{i+1}$ are not divisible by $b_i$.

negatives.text: Let $S$ be a set of $n \ge 3$ positive integers such that the sum of any two distinct elements is not in $S$. Prove that there exists an ordering $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n$ of the elements of $S$ such that for all $i = 2, 3, \dots, n-1$, $b_{i-1} + b_{i+1}$ is divisible by $b_i$.

Prove that there exists an ordering $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n$ of the elements of $S$ such that for all $i = 2, 3, \dots, n-1$, $b_{i-1} + b_{i+1}$ and $b_{i-1} - b_{i+1}$ are not divisible by $b_i$.

positive_text: 令 $k \le n$ 為兩個正整數。數奧國有 $n$ 個村莊, 這些村莊之間可能由道路連接。對於任意兩村莊, 其間的距離為從一村莊到另一村莊所需經過的最少道路數; 若無法從一村莊到達另一村莊, 則距離為無限大。小勳因隔離無法看到村莊間的連接情形, 但他知道 $n$ 和 $k$。他想確認數奧國中最遠的兩個村莊間的距離是否有限。每次他可以打電話到數奧辦公室, 並指定兩村莊, 問它們的距離是否大於、等於或小於 $k$。辦公室會正確回答 (無限大距離視為大於 $k$)。證明小勳可在 $\frac{2n^2}{k}$ 次電話內得知最遠兩村莊間的距離是否有限。

positive_text: Let $n$ and $s$ be positive integers satisfying $s \le 2n^2$. Alice and Bob play a game on a $2n \times 2n$ square grid. Alice assigns a non-negative real number $a_i$ to each cell, where $0 \le a_i \le 1$ and $\sum a_i = s$. Bob then partitions the grid into connected regions (each made of whole cells), such that the total sum of the values in each region is at most 1. Alice wants to maximize the number of regions, and Bob wants to minimize it. Determine the number of regions when both play optimally.

negatives.text: Let $n$ and $k$ be positive integers satisfying $k \le 2n^2$. Lee and Sunny play a game with a $2n \times 2n$ grid paper. Lee writes a non-negative real number no greater than 1 in each cell, so that the sum of all numbers on the paper is $k$. Sunny divides the paper into few pieces such that each piece is constructed by several complete cells, and the sum of all numbers on each piece is at least 1. There are no other restrictions on the shape of each piece. Let $M$ be the final number of pieces. Lee wants to maximize $M$, while Sunny wants to minimize $M$. Find the value of $M$ when both play optimally.

Let $n$ and $k$ be positive integers satisfying $k \le 2n^2$. Lee and Sunny play a game with a $2n \times 2n$ grid paper. Lee writes a non-negative real number in each cell such that the total sum is $k$, with no restriction on the value per cell. Sunny divides the paper into pieces such that the sum of numbers in each piece is at most 1. The number of pieces is $M$. Lee wants to maximize $M$, while Sunny wants to minimize $M$. Find the value of $M$ when both play optimally.

Let $n$ and $k$ be positive integers satisfying $k \le 2n^2$. Lee and Sunny play a game with a $2n \times 2n$ grid paper. Sunny divides the paper into $M$ pieces such that each piece has a total sum of at most 1 and is a $1 \times 1$ square. Lee wants to maximize $M$, while Sunny wants to minimize $M$. Find the value of $M$ when both play optimally.

$$
S_q = \sum_{k=1}^q \frac{1}{(3k-1)(3k)(3k+1)}
$$
Write $1 + 2S_q - \frac{1}{p}$ in the form $\frac{m}{n}$ with $\gcd(m, n) = 1$. Prove that $p$ divides $m$.

$$

$$

positive_text:

$$
f(q) = \begin{cases} q - 3 & \text{if } q \in \mathbb{Z}, \\
\lceil q \rceil - 3 + f\left(\frac{1}{\lceil q \rceil - q}\right) & \text{if } q \notin \mathbb{Z}. 
\end{cases}
$$

Moreover, for any permutation $\{x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n\}$ of $\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$, the $n-1$ matches between $x_1$ and $x_2$, $x_2$ and $x_3$, $\dots$, $x_{n-1}$ and $x_n$ will have at least one winner from each of the $k$ schools. Prove that $n < 2^k$.

positive_text:
Let $\phi = \frac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}$. Find all continuous functions $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that, for all $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
& f(\phi a + b) + f(\phi b + c) + f(\phi c + a) \\
&= \phi f(a + b + c) + 2f(a) + 2f(b) + 2f(c).
\end{aligned}
$$

negatives.text:
Let $\alpha = \frac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}$. Find all continuous functions $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that, for all $x, y, z \in \mathbb{R}$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
& f(\alpha x + y) + f(\alpha y + z) + f(\alpha z + x) \\
&= \alpha f(x + y + z) + 2f(x) + 2f(y) - 2f(z).
\end{aligned}
$$

Let $\alpha = \frac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}$. Find all continuous functions $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that, for all $x, y, z \in \mathbb{R}$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
& f(\alpha x + y) + f(\alpha y + z) + f(\alpha z + x) \\
&= \alpha f(x + y + z) + 2f(x^2) + 2f(y^2) + 2f(z^2).
\end{aligned}
$$

Let $\alpha = \frac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}$. Find all continuous functions $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that, for all $x, y, z \in \mathbb{R}$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
& f(\alpha x + y) + f(\alpha y + z) + f(\alpha z + x) \\

$$

positive_text:
Let $g: \mathbb{R}^+ \to \mathbb{R}^+$ be a function satisfying
$$
(g(ab))^2 = g(a^2)g(b^2)
$$
for all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}^+$ with $a^2b^3 > 2008$. Prove that $(g(ab))^2 = g(a^2)g(b^2)$ for all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}^+$.

negatives.text:
Let $f: \mathbb{R}^+ \to \mathbb{R}^+$ be a function satisfying
$$
(f(xy))^2 = f(x^2) + f(y^2)
$$
for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}^+$ with $x^2y^3 > 2008$. Prove that $(f(xy))^2 = f(x^2) + f(y^2)$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}^+$.

Let $f: \mathbb{R}^+ \to \mathbb{R}^+$ be a function satisfying
$$
(f(xy))^2 = f(x)f(y^2)
$$
for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}^+$ with $x^2y^3 > 2008$. Prove that $(f(xy))^2 = f(x)f(y^2)$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}^+$.

positive_text:
Prove that
$$
\sqrt{x^2 + y^2 - \sqrt{2} xy} + \sqrt{y^2 + z^2 - \sqrt{2} yz} \geq \sqrt{x^2 + z^2}
$$
for all positive real numbers $x$, $y$ and $z$.

negatives.text:

$$
for all positive real numbers $a$, $b$ and $c$.

$$
\sqrt{a^2 + b^2 - ab} + \sqrt{b^2 + c^2 - bc} \geq \sqrt{a^2 + c^2}
$$
for all positive real numbers $a$, $b$ and $c$.

\sqrt{a^2 + b^2 - \sqrt{2} ab} + \sqrt{b^2 + c^2 - \sqrt{2} bc} \geq \sqrt{a^2 + b^2 + c^2}
$$
for all positive real numbers $a$, $b$ and $c$.

positive_text: Let $\{a_n\}_{n \ge 1}$ be a sequence of positive integers such that $a_{n+5} a_n = a_{n+3} a_{n+2}$ for all positive integers $n$. Find the greatest integer that always divides $\sum_{k=1}^{2550} a_{2k-1} a_{2k}$.

negatives.text: Consider the sequence $\{a_n\}_{n \ge 1}$ of positive integers with $a_n a_{n+3} = a_{n+1} a_{n+5}$ for all positive integer $n$. Determine the largest integer that always divides $\sum_{k=1}^{2550} a_{2k} a_{2k-1}$.

Consider the sequence $\{a_n\}_{n \ge 1}$ of positive integers with $a_n a_{n+3} + a_{n+2} a_{n+5} = 0$ for all positive integer $n$. Determine the largest integer that always divides $\sum_{k=1}^{2550} a_{2k} a_{2k-1}$.

Consider the sequence $\{a_n\}_{n \ge 1}$ of positive integers with $a_n a_{n+3} = a_{n+2} a_{n+5} + 1$ for all positive integer $n$. Determine the largest integer that always divides $\sum_{k=1}^{2550} a_{2k} a_{2k-1}$.

positive_text: Let $g: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be such that for all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$, $$ |g(a + b)| = |g(a) + g(b)|\. $$ Prove that $g(a + b) = g(a) + g(b)$ for all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$.

negatives.text: Let $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be such that for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$, $$ |f(x + y)| = |f(x) - f(y)|\. $$ Prove that $f(x + y) = f(x) - f(y)$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$.
Let $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be such that for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$, $$ |f(x + y)| = |f(x) + f(y)| + 1\. $$ Prove that $f(x + y) = f(x) + f(y)$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$.

positive_text: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle with $AB \leq AC$ and let $P$ be an interior point on the bisector of $\angle A$. Let $D, E$ be points on the segments $PC, PB$ respectively such that $\angle PBD = \angle PCE$. The line $BD$ meets $AC$ at $X$, and $CE$ meets $AB$ at $Y$. Prove that $BX \leq CY$.

negatives.text: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle with $AB \leq AC$ and let $P$ be an interior point on the angle bisector of $\angle BAC$. Let $D, E$ be points on the segments $PC, PB$ respectively such that $\angle PBD = \angle PCE$. The line $BD$ meets $AC$ at $X$, and $CE$ meets $AB$ at $Y$. Prove that $BX \geq CY$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle with $AB \leq AC$ and let $P$ be an interior point on the angle bisector of $\angle BAC$. Let $D, E$ be points on the segments $PC, PB$ respectively such that $\angle PBD = 2\angle PCE$. The line $BD$ meets $AC$ at $X$, and $CE$ meets $AB$ at $Y$. Prove that $BX \leq CY$.

positive_text: Let $\omega$ be the incircle of triangle $ABC$, tangent to $BC$ at $D$ and to $AC$ at $E$. Construct a line perpendicular to $BC$ at $D$ intersecting $\omega$ at $P$ (closer to $A$). The line $AP$ meets $BC$ at $M$. Let $N$ be a point on $AC$ with $CN = AE$, and let $BN$ intersect $\omega$ at $Q$ (closer to $B$) and intersect $AM$ at $R$. Prove that the area of triangle $ABR$ equals the area of quadrilateral $PQMN$.

negatives.text: Let $\omega$ be the incircle of triangle $ABC$, tangent to $BC$ at $D$ and to $AC$ at $E$. Draw a line perpendicular to $BC$ at $D$ to intersect $\omega$ at a point $P$ closer to $B$. The line $AP$ meets $BC$ at $M$. Let $N$ be a point on $AC$ such that $AE = CN$, and let $BN$ intersect $\omega$ at a point $Q$ closer to $B$ and intersect $AM$ at $R$. Prove that the area of triangle $ABR$ equals the area of quadrilateral $PQMN$.

Let $\omega$ be the incircle of triangle $ABC$, tangent to $BC$ at $D$ and to $AC$ at $E$. Draw a line perpendicular to $BC$ at $D$ to intersect $\omega$ at a point $P$ closer to $A$. The line $AP$ meets $BC$ at $M$. Let $N$ be a point on $AC$ such that $AE = 2CN$, and let $BN$ intersect $\omega$ at a point $Q$ closer to $B$ and intersect $AM$ at $R$. Prove that the area of triangle $ABR$ equals the area of quadrilateral $PQMN$.

Let $\omega$ be the incircle of triangle $ABC$, tangent to $BC$ at $D$ and to $AC$ at $E$. Draw a line perpendicular to $BC$ at $D$ to intersect $\omega$ at a point $P$ closer to $A$. The line $AP$ meets $BC$ at $M$. Let $N$ be a point on $AC$ such that $AE = CN$, and let $BN$ intersect $\omega$ at a point $Q$ closer to $A$ and intersect $AM$ at $R$. Prove that the area of triangle $ABR$ equals the area of quadrilateral $PQMN$.

positive_text: Let $q(x) = x^{2013} + c_{2012}x^{2012} + c_{2011}x^{2011} + \dots + c_1x + c_0$ be a polynomial with real coefficients. Suppose the roots of $q(x)$ are $$-r_{1006}, -r_{1005}, \dots, -r_1, 0, r_1, \dots, r_{1005}, r_{1006}$$ where $r_1, r_2, \dots, r_{1006}$ are positive real numbers satisfying $r_1r_2\cdots r_{1006} = 1$. Prove that $c_3c_{2011} \geq 1012036$.

negatives.text: Let $p(x) = x^{2013} + a_{2012}x^{2012} + a_{2011}x^{2011} + \dots + a_1x + a_0$ be a polynomial with real coefficients. Suppose that all the roots of $p(x)$ are $$-b_{1006}, -b_{1005}, \dots, -b_1, 0, b_1, \dots, b_{1005}, b_{1006}$$ where $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_{1006}$ are positive real numbers with product equal to $2$. Show that $a_3a_{2011} \geq 1012036$.

Let $p(x) = x^{2013} + a_{2012}x^{2012} + a_{2011}x^{2011} + \dots + a_1x + a_0$ be a polynomial with real coefficients. Suppose that all the roots of $p(x)$ are $$-b_{1006}, -b_{1005}, \dots, -b_1, 0, b_1, \dots, b_{1005}, b_{1006}$$ where $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_{1006}$ are positive real numbers with product equal to $1$. Show that $a_3a_{2010} \geq 1012036$.

Let $p(x) = x^{2013} + a_{2012}x^{2012} + a_{2011}x^{2011} + \dots + a_1x + a_0$ be a polynomial with real coefficients. Suppose that all the roots of $p(x)$ are $$-b_{1006}, -b_{1005}, \dots, -b_1, 0, b_1, \dots, b_{1005}, b_{1006}$$ where $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_{1006}$ are positive real numbers with sum equal to $1$. Show that $a_3a_{2011} \geq 1012036$.

positive_text: Let $M$ and $N$ be positive integers. Mr. Pisut starts at $(0, N)$ and moves to $(M, 0)$ by taking unit-length steps only in the directions of the axes, staying in the first quadrant. For every step along the X-axis, he notes the Y-coordinate at the start of the step if it increases the distance from the origin; otherwise, he notes the negative of that Y-coordinate. For every step along the Y-axis, he similarly records the X-coordinate at the start of the step or its negative. Show that the total of these recorded values is zero.

negatives.text: Let $M$ and $N$ be positive integers. Mr. Pisut starts at $(0, N)$ and walks to $(M, 0)$ with unit-length steps in the directions of the axes. For each step, he records the distance from himself to the origin instead of the axis. If the step moves him farther from the origin, he records the distance as positive; otherwise, negative. Prove that the total of all recorded distances is zero.

Let $M$ and $N$ be positive integers. Mr. Pisut starts at $(0, N)$ and walks to $(M, 0)$ with unit-length steps in the directions of the axes. For each step, he records the distance from himself to the axis to which his step is parallel as positive if the step moves him closer to the origin and negative otherwise. Prove that the total of all recorded distances is zero.

positive_text: Let $k$ be a positive integer. We want to construct a set of cards where each card is labeled with a factorial number $m!$, with $m$ a positive integer. The set must be such that for every integer $s$ satisfying $1 \le s \le k!$, there exists a subset of the cards whose labels sum to $s$. What is the minimum number of cards required in such a set?

negatives.text:
Let $n$ be a positive integer. We want to make up a collection of cards with the following properties:

* for any positive integer $t < n!$, we can select some card(s) from this collection such that the product of the number(s) on the selected card(s) is $t$.
Determine the smallest possible number of cards needed in this collection.

Let $n$ be a positive integer. We want to make up a collection of cards with the following properties:

* for any positive integer $t \le n!$, we can select some card(s) from this collection such that the sum of the number(s) on the selected card(s) is $-t$.
Determine the smallest possible number of cards needed in this collection.

Let $n$ be a positive integer. We want to make up a collection of cards with the following properties:

* for any positive integer $t$ such that $t^2 \le n!$, we can select some card(s) from this collection such that the sum of the number(s) on the selected card(s) is $t$.
Determine the smallest possible number of cards needed in this collection.

positive_text: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB \neq AC$. Let $\ell$ be the internal bisector of $\angle BAC$ and let it intersect $BC$ at $P$ and the perpendicular bisector of $BC$ at $Q$. Prove that $\frac{PQ}{AQ} = \left(\frac{BC}{AB+AC}\right)^2$.

positive_text: Let $p$ be a prime number with $p \ge 5$. Prove that there is some integer $t$ in the range $1 \le t \le p$ for which the equation $$x^2 - y^{\frac{p-1}{2}} = t$$ admits no integer solutions $x$ and $y$.

negatives.text: Let $p \ge 5$ be a positive prime number. Show that for all integers $t \in \{1, 2, ..., p\}$, the equation $$x^2 = y^{\frac{p-1}{2}} + t$$ has integer solutions.

positive_text: Suppose $a$ and $b$ are positive integers. Prove that if $a^{4b+1} - 1$ is prime, then $b$ must be a power of two.

Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers. Prove that if $m^{2n+1} - 1$ is a prime number then there exists an integer $t \ge 0$ such that $n = 2^t$.

positive_text: Is there a mapping $f: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Q}$ such that every rational number $r$ can be uniquely expressed in the form $r = f(m) + \frac{1}{n}$, where $m, n$ are positive integers?

negatives.text: Does there exist a function $f: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Q}$ such that for any rational number $r$, there exists exactly one ordered pair $(m, n)$ of positive integers satisfying the equation $r = f(m) - \frac{1}{n}$?

Does there exist a function $f: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Q}$ such that for any rational number $r$, there exists exactly one ordered pair $(m, n)$ of positive integers satisfying the inequality $r < f(m) + \frac{1}{n}$?

positive_text:
Prove that
$$
\sqrt{x^4 + z^4} + \sqrt{x^4 + w^4} + \sqrt{y^4 + z^4} + \sqrt{y^4 + w^4} \ge 2\sqrt{2}(xw + yz)

for all real numbers $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$.

positive_text: Let there be $n+1$ cities in a country, with bidirectional flights between some pairs. Each bidirectional flight between cities $A$ and $B$ implies a flight in both directions on the same day, and there are no one-way flights. Multiple flights can exist between the same pair of cities. Let $d_A$ be the total number of departures from city $A$ in a day. For all non-capital cities $A$, $d_A \leq n$. Additionally, for any two non-capital cities $A$ and $B$, if there is no bidirectional flight between $A$ and $B$, then $d_A + d_B \leq n$. There is no restriction on the number of flights from the capital. Determine the maximum number of bidirectional flights possible in a day and characterize all such flight configurations.

negatives.text: In a country with $n+1$ cities, there are one-way flights between some cities. Each one-way flight is in only one direction. There may be multiple one-way flights between a pair of cities in each direction. Let $d_A$ denote the total number of departures from city $A$ in a day. For all non-capital cities $A$, $d_A \leq n$. Moreover, for any two non-capital cities $A$ and $B$, if there is no flight in either direction between $A$ and $B$, then $d_A + d_B \leq n$. There is no restriction on the number of flights from the capital. Find the maximum number of one-way flights that can be made in a day.

In a country with $n+1$ cities, there are two-way flights between some of these cities. Each such flight implies flights in both directions within the same day. There may be multiple flights between the same pair of cities. Let $d_A$ be the total number of departures from city $A$ in a day. For all non-capital cities $A$, $d_A \leq n$. Moreover, for any two non-capital cities $A$ and $B$, if there is a two-way flight between them, then $d_A + d_B \leq n$. There is no restriction on the number of flights from the capital. Find the maximum number of two-way flights possible in a day.

positive_text: Let $X$ and $Y$ be distinct points on a circle $\Omega$. For a variable point $Z$ different from $X$ and $Y$ on $\Omega$, find the set of all points $Q$ such that $ZQ$ is the ray opposite to the internal angle bisector of $\angle XZY$ and $QZ = ZX + ZY$.

negatives.text: Let $A$ and $B$ be distinct points on a circle $\Gamma$. For a variable point $P$ different from $A$ and $B$ on $\Gamma$, find the geometric locus of the point $M$ such that $PM$ is the opposite ray to the angle bisector of $\angle APB$ and $MP = |AP - PB|$.

positive_text: Let $\{y_k\}$ be a sequence defined by $y_1 = a$, $y_2 = b$, and $y_k = 2008y_{k-1} - y_{k-2}$ for all $k \ge 2$. Show that there exist positive integers $a$ and $b$ such that for every $k \ge 1$, the value $1 + 2006y_ky_{k+1}$ is a perfect square.

negatives.text: The sequence $\{x_n\}$ is defined by $x_1 = a$, $x_2 = b$ and $x_n = 2008x_{n-1} + x_{n-2}$ for all $n \ge 2$. Prove that there are positive integers $a$ and $b$ such that for all $n \ge 1$ the expression $1 + 2006x_nx_{n+1}$ is a perfect square.
