positive_text: Suppose $n = 6k + 1$ is a prime with $k > 1$. Let $a = 2^n - 1$. Show that $$\frac{2^a - 1}{127a}$$ is an integer.

negatives.text: Let $k > 1$ be an integer and $p = 6k + 1$ be a prime number. Let $m = 2^p + 1$. Prove that $$\frac{2^m - 1}{127m}$$ is an integer.
Let $k > 1$ be an integer and $p = 6k + 1$ be a prime number. Let $m = 2^p - 1$. Prove that $$\frac{2^m + 1}{127m}$$ is an integer.
Let $k > 1$ be an integer and $p = 6k + 1$ be a prime number. Let $m = 2^{p^2} - 1$. Prove that $$\frac{2^m - 1}{127m}$$ is an integer.

positive_text: A network of $2008$ computers is composed of disjoint cycles. At time $t = 0$, one computer is compromised by a hacker. At time $t = 1$, the administrator deploys protection on an uncompromised computer. For each $k \in \mathbb{Z}^+$, at time $t = 2k$, the hacker compromises a new computer adjacent to a compromised one, provided it is not protected; at time $t = 2k + 1$, the administrator protects a new computer adjacent to a protected one, provided it is not compromised. Determine the largest number of computers the hacker can always compromise, regardless of the network structure.

negatives.text: In a network of $2008$ computers with disjoint cycles, the hacker begins at time $t = 0$ and the administrator at $t = 1$. At time $t = 2k$, the hacker compromises a new computer adjacent to a compromised one, provided it is not protected; at time $t = 2k + 1$, the administrator protects a new computer adjacent to a protected one, provided it is not compromised. Determine the maximum number of computers the hacker can compromise if the administrator may also protect computers adjacent to compromised ones.

In a network of $2008$ computers with disjoint cycles, the hacker begins at time $t = 0$ and the administrator at $t = 1$. At time $t = 2k$, the hacker compromises a new computer adjacent to a compromised one, provided it is not protected; at time $t = 2k + 1$, the administrator protects a new computer adjacent to a protected one, provided it is not compromised. Determine the maximum number of computers the hacker can compromise if the administrator may only act at time $t = 2k$.

In a network of $2008$ computers with disjoint cycles, the hacker begins at time $t = 0$ and the administrator at $t = 1$. At time $t = 2k$, the hacker compromises a new computer adjacent to a compromised one, provided it is not protected; at time $t = 2k + 1$, the administrator protects a new computer adjacent to a protected one, provided it is not compromised. Determine the maximum number of computers the hacker can compromise if the administrator may also protect computers not adjacent to any protected ones.

positive_text:
Let triangle $ABC$ have its incircle tangent to $BC$, $AC$, and $AB$ at $A_1$, $B_1$, and $C_1$, respectively. Prove that
$$
\sqrt{|AB_1|} + \sqrt{|BC_1|} + \sqrt{|CA_1|} \le \frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}.
$$

negatives.text:
Let triangle $ABC$ have its incircle tangent to $BC$, $AC$, and $AB$ at $A_1$, $B_1$, and $C_1$, respectively. Prove that
$$
\sqrt{|AB_1|^2} + \sqrt{|BC_1|^2} + \sqrt{|CA_1|^2} \le \frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}.
$$

Let triangle $ABC$ have its incircle tangent to $BC$, $AC$, and $AB$ at $A_1$, $B_1$, and $C_1$, respectively. Prove that
$$
\sqrt{|AB_1|} + \sqrt{|BC_1|} + \sqrt{|CA_1|} \ge \frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}.
$$

Let triangle $ABC$ have its incircle tangent to $BC$, $AC$, and $AB$ at $A_1$, $B_1$, and $C_1$, respectively. Prove that
$$
\sqrt{|AB_1|} + \sqrt{|BC_1|} + \sqrt{|CA_1|} \le 2.
$$

positive_text: Let $n \ge 4$ be an integer. Suppose that among $n$ students in a class, some are friends. For any subset of $n-1$ students, they can be arranged in a circle such that adjacent students in the circle are friends. However, it is impossible to arrange all $n$ students in such a circle. Determine the smallest value of $n$.

negatives.text: Some of $n \ge 4$ students in a class are friends. Any $n-1$ students in this class can form a line so that any two students next to each other on the line are friends, but all $n$ students cannot form a similar line. Find the smallest possible value of $n$.

Some of $n \ge 4$ students in a class are friends. Any $n-1$ students in this class can form a circle so that any two students next to each other on the circle are friends, and all $n$ students can also form a similar circle. Find the smallest possible value of $n$.

Some of $n \ge 4$ students in a class are friends. Any $n-1$ students in this class can form a circle so that any two students next to each other on the circle are not friends, but all $n$ students cannot form a similar circle. Find the smallest possible value of $n$.

positive_text: \text{Let } D, E, F \text{ be points on the sides } AB, BC, CA \text{ respectively of triangle } ABC \text{ such that } AD = AF, BD = BE \text{ and } DE = DF. \text{ Let } I \text{ be the incenter of triangle } ABC, \text{ and let } K \text{ be the point of intersection of the line } BI \text{ and the line tangent to the circumcircle of triangle } ABI \text{ at } A. \text{ Show that } AK = EK \text{ if } AK = AD.

negatives.text: \text{Let } D, E, F \text{ be points on the sides } AB, BC, CA \text{ respectively of triangle } ABC \text{ such that } AD = AF, BD = BE \text{ and } DE = DF. \text{ Let } I \text{ be the incenter of triangle } ABC, \text{ and let } K \text{ be the point of intersection of the line } BI \text{ and the tangent line through } A \text{ to the circumcircle of triangle } AIC. \text{ Show that } AK = EK \text{ if } AK = AD.

\text{Let } D, E, F \text{ be points on the sides } AB, BC, CA \text{ respectively of triangle } ABC \text{ such that } AD = AF, BD = BE \text{ and } DE = DF. \text{ Let } I \text{ be the incenter of triangle } ABC, \text{ and let } K \text{ be the point of intersection of the line } BI \text{ and the tangent line through } A \text{ to the circumcircle of triangle } ABI. \text{ Show that } AK = EK \text{ if } AK = AD + 1.

positive_text:
Prove that
$$
\sum_{k=1}^{n} \frac{x_k}{\sqrt{x_k^4 + 3}} \le \frac{1}{2} \sum_{k=1}^{n} \frac{1}{x_k}
$$
for all positive integers $n$ and positive real numbers $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n$ with the condition that $x_1 x_2 \cdots x_n = 1$.

negatives.text:
Show that
$$
\sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{a_i}{\sqrt{a_i^4 - 3}} \le \frac{1}{2} \sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{1}{a_i}
$$
for all positive integers $n$ and positive real numbers $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ such that $a_1 a_2 \cdots a_n = 1$.

Prove that
$$
\sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{a_i}{\sqrt{a_i^2 + 3}} \le \frac{1}{2} \sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{1}{a_i}
$$
for all positive integers $n$ and positive real numbers $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ such that $a_1 a_2 \cdots a_n = 1$.

Show that
$$
\sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{a_i}{\sqrt{a_i^4 + 3}} \ge \frac{1}{2} \sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{1}{a_i}
$$
for all positive integers $n$ and positive real numbers $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ such that $a_1 a_2 \cdots a_n = 1$.

positive_text: \text{Prove that } x^2 y^2 (x^2 + y^2 - 2) \geq (x + y)(xy - 1) \text{ for all positive real numbers } x \text{ and } y.

negatives.text: \text{Prove that } a^2 b^2 (a^2 + b^2 - 2) \leq (a + b)(ab - 1) \text{ for all positive real numbers } a \text{ and } b.
\text{Prove that } a^2 b^2 (a^2 + b^2 + 2) \geq (a + b)(ab - 1) \text{ for all positive real numbers } a \text{ and } b.
\text{Prove that } a^2 b^2 (a^2 + b^2 - 2) \geq (a + b)(ab + 1) \text{ for all positive real numbers } a \text{ and } b.

positive_text: Let $n \ge 2$ be an integer and $E = \{1, 2, \dots, n\}$. Suppose $S_1, S_2, \dots, S_k$ are subsets of $E$ such that for every pair $i < j$, exactly one of the four intersections $S_i \cap S_j$, $S_i^c \cap S_j$, $S_i \cap S_j^c$, and $S_i^c \cap S_j^c$ is empty. What is the largest possible value of $k$?

negatives.text: Let $n \ge 2$ be an integer and $E = \{1, 2, \dots, n\}$. Suppose $A_1, A_2, \dots, A_k$ are subsets of $E$ such that for every pair $i < j$, at least one of $A_i \cap A_j$, $A'_i \cap A_j$, $A_i \cap A'_j$, and $A'_i \cap A'_j$ is empty. What is the maximum value of $k$?

Let $n \ge 2$ be an integer and $E = \{1, 2, \dots, n\}$. Suppose $A_1, A_2, \dots, A_k$ are subsets of $E$ such that for every pair $i < j$, exactly one of $A_i \cup A_j$, $A'_i \cup A_j$, $A_i \cup A'_j$, and $A'_i \cup A'_j$ is empty. What is the maximum value of $k$?

positive_text: Let $ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $AB = AC$. Let $D$ be the midpoint of segment $BC$, and let $E$ be the projection of $D$ onto $AC$. Suppose $F$ is the second intersection of line $BE$ with the circumcircle of triangle $ABD$, and let $G$ be the intersection of lines $DE$ and $AF$. Prove that $DG = GE$.

negatives.text: In triangle $ABC$, $|AB| = |AC|$, and $D$ is the midpoint of $[BC]$. Let $E$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $C$ to $AC$. If $F$ is the second point of intersection of $BE$ with the circumcircle of triangle $ABD$, and $G$ is the intersection of lines $DE$ and $AF$, show that $|DG| = |GE|$.

Let triangle $ABC$ be isosceles with $AB = AC$, and let $D$ be the midpoint of $BC$. Let $E$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $D$ to $AB$ instead of $AC$. Suppose $F$ is the second point of intersection of $BE$ with the circumcircle of triangle $ABD$, and $G$ is the intersection of $DE$ and $AF$. Prove that $DG = GE$.

In triangle $ABC$, $|AB| = |AC|$, and $D$ is the midpoint of $[BC]$. Let $E$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $D$ to the line $AC$, and let $F$ be the second point where the line $EC$ intersects the circumcircle of triangle $ABD$. If $G$ is the intersection of $DE$ and $AF$, prove that $|DG| = |GE|$.

positive_text:
Prove that
$$
x + y + z + \sqrt{3} \geq 8xyz \left( \frac{1}{x^2 + 1} + \frac{1}{y^2 + 1} + \frac{1}{z^2 + 1} \right)
$$
for all positive real numbers $x, y, z$ such that $xy + yz + zx \leq 1$.

negatives.text:
Show that
$$
a + b + c + \sqrt{3} \leq 8abc \left( \frac{1}{a^2 + 1} + \frac{1}{b^2 + 1} + \frac{1}{c^2 + 1} \right)
$$
for all positive real numbers $a, b, c$ satisfying $ab + bc + ca \leq 1$.

Show that
$$
a + b + c + \sqrt{3} \geq 8abc \left( \frac{1}{a^3 + 1} + \frac{1}{b^3 + 1} + \frac{1}{c^3 + 1} \right)
$$
for all positive real numbers $a, b, c$ satisfying $ab + bc + ca \leq 1$.

positive_text:
Prove that
$$
\frac{1}{a + b^{20} + c^{11}} + \frac{1}{b + c^{20} + a^{11}} + \frac{1}{c + a^{20} + b^{11}} \le 1
$$
for all positive real numbers $a, b, c$ such that $abc = 1$.

negatives.text:
Show that
$$
\frac{1}{x + y^{20} + z^{11}} + \frac{1}{y + z^{20} + x^{11}} + \frac{1}{z + x^{20} + y^{11}} \ge 1
$$
for all positive real numbers $x, y, z$ satisfying $xyz = 1$.

Prove that
$$
\frac{1}{x + y^{20} + z^{11}} + \frac{1}{y + z^{20} + x^{11}} + \frac{1}{z + x^{20} + y^{11}} \le 1
$$
for all positive real numbers $x, y, z$ satisfying $x + y + z = 3$.

Show that
$$
\frac{1}{x + y^{20} + z^{11}} + \frac{1}{y + z^{20} + x^{11}} + \frac{1}{z + x^{20} + y^{11}} \le 1
$$
for all positive real numbers $x, y, z$ satisfying $xyz = 2$.

positive_text: Let $T_r(n) = 1^r + 2^r + \dots + n^r$ where $r$ is a rational number and $n$ is a positive integer. Determine all triples $(x, y, z)$ with $x$ and $y$ positive rational numbers and $z$ a positive integer such that there are infinitely many positive integers $n$ for which $T_x(n) = (T_y(n))^z$.

negatives.text: Let $S_r(n) = 1^r + 2^r + \dots + n^r$ where $r$ is a rational number and $n$ is a positive integer. Find all triples $(a, b, c)$ where $a$ and $b$ are positive rational numbers and $c$ is a positive integer for which there exist infinitely many positive integers $n$ satisfying $S_a(n) = c(S_b(n))$.

Let $S_r(n) = 1^r + 2^r + \dots + n^r$ where $r$ is a rational number and $n$ is a positive integer. Find all triples $(a, b, c)$ where $a$ and $b$ are positive rational numbers and $c$ is a positive integer for which there exist infinitely many positive integers $n$ satisfying $S_a(n) = (S_b(n))^{1/c}$.

Let $S_r(n) = 1^r + 2^r + \dots + n^r$ where $r$ is a rational number and $n$ is a positive integer. Find all triples $(a, b, c)$ where $a$ and $b$ are positive rational numbers and $c$ is a positive integer for which there exist infinitely many positive integers $n$ satisfying $S_a(n) + (S_b(n))^c = 0$.

positive_text:
Determine all integer pairs $(a, b)$ and prime $q$ such that
$$
a^2 - 3ab + q^2b^2 = 12q.
$$

negatives.text:
Find all triples $(x, y, p)$ satisfying
$$
x^2 + 3xy + p^2y^2 = 12p
$$
where $x, y$ are integers and $p$ is a prime number.

Find all triples $(x, y, p)$ satisfying
$$
x^2 - 3xy + p^2y^2 = -12p
$$
where $x, y$ are integers and $p$ is a prime number.

Find all triples $(x, y, p)$ satisfying
$$
x^2 - 3xy + p^2y^2 = 12p^2
$$
where $x, y$ are integers and $p$ is a prime number.

positive_text: Let $P$ be the set of all $n$-tuples $(x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n)$, where $x_i \in \{1, 2, \dots, m\}$ for each $1 \le i \le n$. The set $A \subset P$ is said to be decreasing if for each $(x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n) \in A$ any $(y_1, y_2, \dots, y_n)$ satisfying $y_i \le x_i$ ($1 \le i \le n$) also belongs to $A$. The set $B \subset P$ is said to be increasing if for each $(x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n) \in B$ any $(y_1, y_2, \dots, y_n)$ satisfying $y_i \ge x_i$ ($1 \le i \le n$) also belongs to $B$. Find the maximal possible value of $f(A, B) = \frac{|A \cap B|}{|A| \cdot |B|}$, where $A$ and $B$ are nonempty decreasing and increasing sets ($| \cdot |$ denotes the number of elements of the set). Here, $n = 2012$ and $m = 20$.

negatives.text: Let $P$ be the set of all $2012$-tuples $(x_1, x_2, \dots, x_{2012})$, where $x_i \in \{1, 2, \dots, 20\}$ for each $1 \le i \le 2012$. The set $A \subset P$ is said to be decreasing if for each $(x_1, x_2, \dots, x_{2012}) \in A$ any $(y_1, y_2, \dots, y_{2012})$ satisfying $y_i < x_i$ ($1 \le i \le 2012$) also belongs to $A$. The set $B \subset P$ is said to be increasing if for each $(x_1, x_2, \dots, x_{2012}) \in B$ any $(y_1, y_2, \dots, y_{2012})$ satisfying $y_i > x_i$ ($1 \le i \le 2012$) also belongs to $B$. Find the maximal possible value of $f(A, B) = \frac{|A \cap B|}{|A| \cdot |B|}$, where $A$ and $B$ are nonempty decreasing and increasing sets.

Let $P$ be the set of all $2012$-tuples $(x_1, x_2, \dots, x_{2012})$, where $x_i \in \{1, 2, \dots, 20\}$ for each $1 \le i \le 2012$. The set $A \subset P$ is said to be decreasing if for each $(x_1, x_2, \dots, x_{2012}) \in A$ any $(y_1, y_2, \dots, y_{2012})$ satisfying $y_i \le x_i$ ($1 \le i \le 2012$) also belongs to $A$. The set $B \subset P$ is said to be increasing if for each $(x_1, x_2, \dots, x_{2012}) \in B$ any $(y_1, y_2, \dots, y_{2012})$ satisfying $y_i \ge x_i$ ($1 \le i \le 2012$) also belongs to $B$. Find the maximal possible value of $f(A, B) = \frac{|A \cup B|}{|A| \cdot |B|}$, where $A$ and $B$ are nonempty decreasing and increasing sets.

Let $P$ be the set of all $2012$-tuples $(x_1, x_2, \dots, x_{2012})$, where $x_i \in \{1, 2, \dots, 20\}$ for each $1 \le i \le 2012$. The set $A \subset P$ is said to be decreasing if for each $(x_1, x_2, \dots, x_{2012}) \in A$ any $(y_1, y_2, \dots, y_{2012})$ satisfying $y_i \le x_i$ ($1 \le i \le 2012$) also belongs to $A$. The set $B \subset P$ is said to be increasing if for each $(x_1, x_2, \dots, x_{2012}) \in B$ any $(y_1, y_2, \dots, y_{2012})$ satisfying $y_i \ge x_i$ ($1 \le i \le 2012$) also belongs to $B$. Find the maximal possible value of $f(A, B) = \frac{|A \cap B|}{|A| + |B|}$, where $A$ and $B$ are nonempty decreasing and increasing sets.

positive_text: Let $\omega_1$ be a circle with diameter $[AB]$ and $\omega_2$ a circle centered at $A$ that intersects $\omega_1$ at points $C$ and $D$. Let $E$ be a point on $\omega_2$ outside $\omega_1$, on the same side of $AB$ as $C$. The line $BE$ intersects $\omega_2$ again at $F$. Let $K$ be a point on $\omega_1$, on the same side of the diameter through $C$ as $A$, satisfying $2 \cdot CK \cdot AC = CE \cdot AB$. Let the second point of intersection of $KF$ with $\omega_1$ be $L$. Prove that the reflection of $D$ across $BE$ lies on the circumcircle of triangle $LFC$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AC > AB$. A circle $\omega$ is tangent to $AB$ at $D$ and $AC$ at $E$, and intersects the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$ at $K$ and $L$. Define $X$ on $AB$ and $Y$ on $AC$ so that
$$
\frac{AX}{AB} = \frac{CE}{BD + CE} \quad \text{and} \quad \frac{AY}{AC} = \frac{BD}{BD + CE}.
$$
Prove that $XY$, $BC$, and $KL$ are concurrent.

negatives.text:
Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AC > AB$. A circle $\omega$ is tangent to $AB$ at $D$ and $AC$ at $E$, and intersects the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$ at $K$ and $L$. Define $X$ on $AB$ and $Y$ on $AC$ so that
$$
\frac{AX}{AB} = \frac{BD}{BD + CE} \quad \text{and} \quad \frac{AY}{AC} = \frac{CE}{BD + CE}.
$$
Prove that $XY$, $BC$, and $KL$ are concurrent.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AC > AB$. A circle $\omega$ is tangent to $AB$ at $D$ and $AC$ at $E$, and intersects the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$ at $K$ and $L$. Define $X$ on $AB$ and $Y$ on $AC$ so that
$$
\frac{AX}{AB} = \frac{CE}{BD - CE} \quad \text{and} \quad \frac{AY}{AC} = \frac{BD}{BD + CE}.
$$
Prove that $XY$, $BC$, and $KL$ are concurrent.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AC > AB$. A circle $\omega$ is tangent to $AB$ at $D$ and $AC$ at $E$, and intersects the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$ at $K$ and $L$. Define $X$ on $AB$ and $Y$ on $AC$ so that
$$
\frac{AX}{AB} = \frac{CE^2}{BD + CE} \quad \text{and} \quad \frac{AY}{AC} = \frac{BD}{BD + CE}.
$$
Prove that $XY$, $BC$, and $KL$ are concurrent.

positive_text:
Let $p > 1$, $q > 1$, $r > 1$, $s > 1$, $m$, $n$ be real numbers satisfying
$$
 p^m + q^n = (p^2 + q^2)^m \text{ and } r^m + s^n = 2^n (rs)^{n/2}.
$$
Prove that $m < n$.

negatives.text:
Let $a > 1$, $b > 1$, $c > 1$, $d > 1$, $x$, $y$ be real numbers satisfying
$$
 a^x + b^y = (a^2 + b^2)^y \text{ and } c^x + d^y = 2^x (cd)^{y/2}.
$$
Prove that $x < y$.

Let $a > 1$, $b > 1$, $c > 1$, $d > 1$, $x$, $y$ be real numbers satisfying
$$
 a^x + b^x = (a^2 + b^2)^x \text{ and } c^x + d^y = 2^y (cd)^{y/2}.
$$
Prove that $x < y$.

Let $a > 1$, $b > 1$, $c > 1$, $d > 1$, $x$, $y$ be real numbers satisfying
$$
 a^x + b^y = (a^2 + b^2)^x \text{ and } c^x + d^y = 2^x (cd)^{x/2}.
$$
Prove that $x < y$.

positive_text:
Let a line $ l $ meet the line $ AB $ at $ F $, the sides $ AC $ and $ BC $ of triangle $ ABC $ at points $ D $ and $ E $, respectively, and the angle bisector of $ \angle BAC $ at $ P $. Assume $ F $ lies on the side of $ AB $ opposite to $ A $ with respect to $ BC $, that $ CD = CE $, and that $ P $ lies inside triangle $ ABC $. Prove that
$$
FB \cdot FA + CP^2 = CF^2 \iff AD \cdot BE = PD^2.
$$

negatives.text:
Let a line $ l $ intersect the line $ AB $ at $ F $, the sides $ AC $ and $ BC $ of a triangle $ ABC $ at $ D $ and $ E $, respectively, and the internal bisector of the angle $ BAC $ at $ P $. Suppose that $ F $ is at the opposite side of $ A $ with respect to the line $ BC $, $ CD = 2CE $, and $ P $ is in the interior of the triangle $ ABC $. Prove that
$$
FB \cdot FA + CP^2 = CF^2 \iff AD \cdot BE = PD^2.
$$

Let a line $ l $ intersect the line $ AB $ at $ F $, the sides $ AC $ and $ BC $ of a triangle $ ABC $ at $ D $ and $ E $, respectively, and the internal bisector of the angle $ BAC $ at $ P $. Suppose that $ F $ is at the opposite side of $ A $ with respect to the line $ BC $, $ CD = CE $, and $ P $ is in the interior of the triangle $ ABC $. Prove that
$$
FB \cdot FA - CP^2 = CF^2 \iff AD \cdot BE = PD^2.
$$

positive_text: \text{Find the minimal possible value of } \frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{y} + \frac{1}{z} \text{ over all positive real numbers } x, y, z \text{ satisfying } xyz = 1, \quad x + y + z = 5 \text{ and } (xy + 2x + 2y - 9)(yz + 2y + 2z - 9)(zx + 2z + 2x - 9) \geq 0.

negatives.text: \text{Find the minimal possible value of } \frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{b} + \frac{1}{c} \text{ over all positive real numbers } a, b, c \text{ satisfying } abc = 1, \quad a + b + c = 5 \text{ and } (ab + 2a + 2b + 9)(bc + 2b + 2c + 9)(ca + 2c + 2a + 9) \geq 0.

\text{Find the minimal possible value of } \frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{b} + \frac{1}{c} \text{ over all positive real numbers } a, b, c \text{ satisfying } abc = 1, \quad a + b + c = 5 \text{ and } (ab + 2a + 2b - 9)(bc + 2b + 2c - 9)(ca + 2c + 2a - 9) \leq 0.

\text{Find the minimal possible value of } \frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{b} + \frac{1}{c} \text{ over all positive real numbers } a, b, c \text{ satisfying } abc = 1, \quad a + b + c = 5 \text{ and } (ab + 2a^2 + 2b - 9)(bc + 2b + 2c - 9)(ca + 2c + 2a - 9) \geq 0.

positive_text: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $|AB| = |AC|$. Let $\omega$ be the circumcircle of $ABC$, and let $D$ be a point on the minor arc $AC$ of $\omega$. Let $E$ be the reflection of $B$ over the line $AD$. The line $BE$ meets $\omega$ again at $F$. The tangent to $\omega$ at $F$ intersects $AC$ at $K$, and the lines $DF$ and $AB$ intersect at $L$. Prove that $K$, $L$, and $E$ lie on a straight line.

negatives.text: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $|AB| = |AC|$. Let $\omega$ be the circumcircle of $ABC$, and let $D$ be a point on the major arc $AC$ of $\omega$. Let $E$ be the reflection of $B$ over the line $AD$. The line $BE$ meets $\omega$ again at $F$. The tangent to $\omega$ at $F$ intersects $AC$ at $K$, and the lines $DF$ and $AB$ intersect at $L$. Prove that $K$, $L$, and $E$ are collinear.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $|AB| = |AC|$. Let $\omega$ be the circumcircle of $ABC$, and let $D$ be a point on the minor arc $AC$ of $\omega$. Let $E$ be the reflection of $A$ over the line $BD$. The line $BE$ meets $\omega$ again at $F$. The tangent to $\omega$ at $F$ intersects $AC$ at $K$, and the lines $DF$ and $AB$ intersect at $L$. Prove that $K$, $L$, and $E$ are collinear.

positive_text: Let triangle $ABC$ satisfy $AB > AC$. Let $D$ lie on segment $BC$ such that $AD$ is perpendicular to $BC$. Let $K$ be the point where $AD$ meets the angle bisector of $\angle ABC$. Let $M$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $B$ to $CK$, and let $N$ be the point where $BM$ meets $AK$. Let $T$ be the intersection of $AC$ with the line through $N$ parallel to $DM$. Prove that $BM$ bisects $\angle TBC$.

negatives.text: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $|AB| > |AC|$. Let $D$ be the foot of the altitude drawn from $A$ to $BC$, $K$ be the intersection of $AD$ and the external bisector of the angle at $B$, $M$ be the foot of the perpendicular drawn from $B$ to $CK$ and $N$ be the intersection of $BM$ and $AK$. Let $T$ be the intersection of $AC$ with the line which passes through $N$ and is parallel to $DM$. Show that $BM$ is the internal bisector of the angle $\angle TBC$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $|AB| > |AC|$. Let $D$ be the foot of the altitude drawn from $A$ to $BC$, $K$ be the intersection of $AD$ and the internal bisector of the angle at $B$, $M$ be the foot of the perpendicular drawn from $C$ to $BK$ and $N$ be the intersection of $BM$ and $AK$. Let $T$ be the intersection of $AC$ with the line which passes through $N$ and is parallel to $DM$. Show that $BM$ is the internal bisector of the angle $\angle TBC$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $|AB| > |AC|$. Let $D$ be the foot of the altitude drawn from $A$ to $BC$, $K$ be the intersection of $AD$ and the internal bisector of the angle at $B$, $M$ be the foot of the perpendicular drawn from $B$ to $CK$ and $N$ be the intersection of $BM$ and $AK$. Let $T$ be the intersection of $AB$ with the line which passes through $N$ and is parallel to $DM$. Show that $BM$ is the internal bisector of the angle $\angle TBC$.

positive_text: Let triangle $ABC$ have $\angle C = 90^\circ$, and let $D$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $C$ to $AB$. Let $E$ and $F$ be the reflections of $D$ across $AC$ and $BC$, respectively. Let $O_1$ and $O_2$ be the centers of the circumcircles of triangles $ECB$ and $FCA$, respectively. Show that $$ 2|O_1O_2| = |AB|. $$

negatives.text: In triangle $ABC$ with $\angle C = 90^\circ$, let $D$ be the foot of the altitude from $C$. Let $E$ and $F$ be the reflections of $D$ with respect to $AC$ and $AB$, respectively. Let $O_1$ and $O_2$ be the circumcenters of triangles $ECB$ and $FCA$, respectively. Prove that $$ 2|O_1O_2| = |AB|. $$

Let triangle $ABC$ have $\angle C = 90^\circ$, and let $D$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $C$ to $AB$. Let $E$ and $F$ be the reflections of $D$ across $AC$ and $BC$, respectively. Let $O_1$ and $O_2$ be the centers of the circumcircles of triangles $ECB$ and $FCA$, respectively. Prove that $$ |O_1O_2| = |AB|. $$

In triangle $ABC$ with $\angle C = 90^\circ$, let $D$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $C$ to $AB$. Let $E$ and $F$ be the reflections of $D$ with respect to $AC$ and $BC$, respectively. Let $O_1$ and $O_2$ be the circumcenters of triangles $ECB$ and $FCA$, respectively. Prove that $$ |O_1O_2| = \frac{1}{3}|AB|. $$

positive_text: Let $q$ be an odd prime number, $a > 1$ and $k$ be positive integers such that $\frac{a^{qk} - 1}{a^k - 1}$ is a prime number. Prove that $$ qk \mid (q-1)^k + 1. $$

negatives.text: Let $p$ be an odd prime number, $m > 1$ and $n$ be positive integers such that $\frac{m^{pn} + 1}{m^n + 1}$ is a prime number. Show that $$ pn \mid (p-1)^n + 1. $$
Let $p$ be an odd prime number, $m > 1$ and $n$ be positive integers such that $\frac{m^{p(n+1)} - 1}{m^n - 1}$ is a prime number. Show that $$ pn \mid (p-1)^n + 1. $$

positive_text: Let triangle $ABC$ have $\angle B < \angle C$, and let $K$ be the excenter opposite $B$, tangent to side $AC$. Suppose $AK$ meets $BC$ at point $D$, and let $E$ be the circumcenter of triangle $BKC$. Show that $$ \frac{1}{|KA|} = \frac{1}{|KD|} + \frac{1}{|KE|}. $$

negatives.text: In triangle $ABC$ with $\angle B < \angle C$, let $K$ be the incenter of triangle $ABC$. The lines $AK$ and $BC$ meet at $D$, and $E$ is the circumcenter of triangle $BKC$. Prove that $$ \frac{1}{|KA|} = \frac{1}{|KD|} + \frac{1}{|KE|}. $$

In triangle $ABC$ with $\angle B < \angle C$, let $K$ be the excenter tangent to side $AC$. The lines $BK$ and $AC$ intersect at $D$, and $E$ is the circumcenter of triangle $BKC$. Prove that $$ \frac{1}{|KA|} = \frac{1}{|KD|} + \frac{1}{|KE|}. $$

Let triangle $ABC$ have $\angle B < \angle C$, and let $K$ be the excenter tangent to side $AC$. The lines $AK$ and $BC$ intersect at $D$, and $E$ is the centroid of triangle $BKC$. Prove that $$ \frac{1}{|KA|} = \frac{1}{|KD|} + \frac{1}{|KE|}. $$

positive_text:
Determine all integer solutions $(x, m, q)$ to the equation
$$
|6x^2 - 17x - 39| = q^m
$$
where $x, m$ are integers and $q$ is a prime.

negatives.text:
Find all triples $(n, k, p)$ satisfying the equation
$$
6n^2 - 17n - 39 = p^k
$$
where $n, k$ are integers and $p$ is a prime.

Find all triples $(n, k, p)$ satisfying the equation
$$
|6n^2 + 17n - 39| = p^k
$$
where $n, k$ are integers and $p$ is a prime.

Find all triples $(n, k, p)$ satisfying the equation
$$
|6n^3 - 17n - 39| = p^k
$$
where $n, k$ are integers and $p$ is a prime.

positive_text:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a collection of $n$ distinct subsets of a universal set, each of cardinality $k$, with the property that for all $A, B \in \mathcal{F}$ with $A \neq B$, the symmetric difference $A \Delta B$ is also an element of $\mathcal{F}$.

a) Is it possible that $n = 2023$? If so, determine all values of $k$ that satisfy this condition.

b) Is it possible that $n = 1023$? If so, determine all values of $k$ that satisfy this condition.

negatives.text:
Let $\mathcal{S}$ be a family of $n$ sets, each of size $k$, such that $A \cap B \in \mathcal{S}$ whenever $A, B \in \mathcal{S}, A \neq B$.

a) Is it possible that $n = 2023$? If it is, find all possible values of $k$.

b) Is it possible that $n = 1023$? If it is, find all possible values of $k$.

Let $\mathcal{S}$ be a family of $n$ sets, each of size $k$, such that $A \Delta B \in \mathcal{S}$ whenever $A, B \in \mathcal{S}, A \neq B$, and $k$ is even.

a) Is it possible that $n = 2023$? If it is, find all possible values of $k$.

b) Is it possible that $n = 1023$? If it is, find all possible values of $k$.

positive_text:
Let $n \ge 3$ be an integer and $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n$ be real numbers. For each $1 \le k \le n$ the real numbers $y_1, y_2, \dots, y_{n+1}$ are defined by
$$
 y_k = \frac{x_k + \max\{x_{k+1}, x_{k+2}\}}{2}
$$
and $y_{n+1} = y_1$ ($x_{n+1} = x_1$ and $x_{n+2} = x_2$). Find the smallest $\mu$ such that the inequality
$$
 \mu \left[ \sum_{i=1}^{n} (x_i - x_{i+1})^{2024} \right] \geq \sum_{i=1}^{n} (y_i - y_{i+1})^{2024}
$$
is satisfied for each $n \ge 3$ and all real numbers $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n$.

negatives.text:
Let $n \ge 3$ be an integer and $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ be real numbers. For each $1 \le k \le n$ the real numbers $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_{n+1}$ are defined by
$$
 b_k = \frac{a_k + \max\{a_{k+1}, a_{k+2}\}}{2}
$$
and $b_{n+1} = b_1$ ($a_{n+1} = a_1$ and $a_{n+2} = a_2$). Find the smallest $\lambda$ such that the inequality
$$
 \lambda \left[ \sum_{i=1}^{n} |a_i - a_{i+1}|^{2024} \right] \geq \sum_{i=1}^{n} |b_i - b_{i+1}|^{2024}
$$
is held for each $n \ge 3$ and all real numbers $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$.

positive_text:
Let $\sigma(n)$ denote the sum of the positive divisors of a positive integer $n$. Define a sequence $(b_i)_{i=0}^{\infty}$ by $b_0 = 1$, and for $i > 0$, let $b_i$ be the smallest integer greater than 1 such that
$$
\sigma(b_0 b_1 \cdots b_{i-1}) \mid \sigma(b_0 b_1 \cdots b_i).
$$
Find how many elements of the sequence divide $2024^{2024}$.

negatives.text:
Let $\sigma(n)$ denote the sum of the positive divisors of a positive integer $n$. Define a sequence $(a_i)_{i=0}^{\infty}$ with $a_0 = 1$, and for $i > 0$, let $a_i$ be the smallest integer greater than 1 such that
$$
\sigma(a_0 a_1 \cdots a_{i-1}) \mid a_0 a_1 \cdots a_i.
$$
Determine how many elements of the sequence divide $2024^{2024}$.

Let $\sigma(n)$ denote the sum of the positive divisors of a positive integer $n$. Define a sequence $(a_i)_{i=0}^{\infty}$ by $a_0 = 1$, and for $i > 0$, let $a_i$ be the smallest integer greater than 1 such that
$$
\sigma(a_0 a_1 \cdots a_i) \mid \sigma(a_0 a_1 \cdots a_{i-1}).
$$
Determine how many elements of the sequence divide $2024^{2024}$.

Let $\sigma(n)$ denote the sum of the positive divisors of a positive integer $n$. Define a sequence $(a_i)_{i=0}^{\infty}$ by $a_0 = 1$, and for $i > 0$, let $a_i$ be the smallest integer greater than 1 such that
$$
\sigma(a_0 a_1 \cdots a_{i-1}) < \sigma(a_0 a_1 \cdots a_i).
$$
Determine how many elements of the sequence divide $2024^{2024}$.

positive_text:
Let $x, y, z \in [0; \frac{\pi}{2}]$ be angles such that
$$
\sin x + \sin y + \sin z = 1, \quad \sum_{cyc} \sin x \cos 2x = -1.
$$
Determine all possible values of $\sin^2 x + \sin^2 y + \sin^2 z$.

negatives.text:
Let $\alpha, \beta, \gamma \in [0; \frac{\pi}{2}]$ satisfy the conditions
$$
\sin \alpha + \sin \beta + \sin \gamma = 1, \quad \sin \alpha \cos 2\alpha + \sin \beta \cos 2\beta + \sin \gamma \cos 2\gamma = 1.
$$
Find all the possible values of $\sin^2 \alpha + \sin^2 \beta + \sin^2 \gamma$.

Let $\alpha, \beta, \gamma \in [0; \frac{\pi}{2}]$ satisfy the conditions
$$
\sin \alpha + \sin \beta + \sin \gamma = 1, \quad \sin^2 \alpha \cos 2\alpha + \sin^2 \beta \cos 2\beta + \sin^2 \gamma \cos 2\gamma = -1.
$$
Find all the possible values of $\sin^2 \alpha + \sin^2 \beta + \sin^2 \gamma$.

Let $\alpha, \beta, \gamma \in [0; \frac{\pi}{2}]$ satisfy the conditions
$$
\sin \alpha + \sin \beta + \sin \gamma = 1, \quad \sin \alpha \cos 3\alpha + \sin \beta \cos 3\beta + \sin \gamma \cos 3\gamma = -1.
$$
Find all the possible values of $\sin^2 \alpha + \sin^2 \beta + \sin^2 \gamma$.

positive_text: Suppose we have $n$ ($n \ge 3$) points in the plane not all collinear. Define $f(P)$ for a point $P$ as the total distance from $P$ to each of these $n$ points. If there exists a point $P_0$ such that $f(P_0) \le f(P)$ for all $P$ in the plane, and another point $P_1$ with $f(P_0) = f(P_1)$, prove that $P_0 = P_1$.

negatives.text: Suppose we have $n$ ($n \ge 3$) points in the plane not all collinear. Define $f(P)$ for a point $P$ as the sum of the squares of the distances from $P$ to each of these $n$ points. If there exists a point $P_0$ such that $f(P_0) \le f(P)$ for all $P$ in the plane, and another point $P_1$ with $f(P_0) = f(P_1)$, prove that $P_0 = P_1$.

Suppose we have $n$ ($n \ge 3$) points in the plane not all collinear. Define $f(P)$ for a point $P$ as the sum of the distances from $P$ to each of these $n$ points. If there exists a point $P_0$ such that $f(P_0) \le f(P)$ for all $P$ in the plane, and another point $P_1$ with $f(P_0) < f(P_1)$, prove that $P_0 = P_1$.

positive_text:
Show that for all $n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$, the sum
$$
\sum_{k=1}^{n} \frac{k+2}{k! + (k+1)! + (k+2)!}
$$
is strictly less than $\frac{1}{2}$.

negatives.text:
Prove that for every positive integer $n$ the inequality
$$
\frac{3}{1!+ 2!+ 3!} + \frac{4}{2!+ 3!+ 4!} + \dots + \frac{n+2}{n!+ (n+1)!+ (n+2)!} > \frac{1}{2}
$$
holds.

Prove that for every positive integer $n$ the inequality
$$
\frac{3}{(1!)^2+ (2!)^2+ (3!)^2} + \frac{4}{(2!)^2+ (3!)^2+ (4!)^2} + \dots + \frac{n+2}{(n!)^2+ ((n+1)!)^2+ ((n+2)!)^2} < \frac{1}{2}
$$
holds.

Prove that for every positive integer $n$ the inequality
$$
\frac{3}{1!+ 2!+ 3!} + \frac{4}{2!+ 3!+ 4!} + \dots + \frac{n+2}{n!+ (n+1)!+ (n+2)!} < \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{n}
$$
holds.

positive_text: \text{a) Determine all real numbers } x \text{ satisfying } x^2 + \frac{1}{x(x + 2)} = 1\\\text{b) Determine all pairs of positive real numbers } x \text{ and } y \text{ satisfying } x^2 + y^2 + \frac{1}{x(x + 2)} + \frac{1}{y(y + 2)} = 2

negatives.text: \text{a) Find all real numbers } x \text{ such that } x^2 + \frac{1}{x^2 - 2x} = 1\\\text{b) Find all pairs of positive real numbers } x \text{ and } y \text{ such that } x^2 + y^2 + \frac{1}{x^2 - 2x} + \frac{1}{y^2 - 2y} = 2

\text{a) Find all real numbers } x \text{ such that } x^2 + \left(\frac{1}{x^2 + 2x}\right)^2 = 1\\\text{b) Find all pairs of positive real numbers } x \text{ and } y \text{ such that } x^2 + y^2 + \left(\frac{1}{x^2 + 2x}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{1}{y^2 + 2y}\right)^2 = 2

\text{a) Find all real numbers } x \text{ such that } x^2 + \frac{1}{x^2 + 2x} = -1\\\text{b) Find all pairs of positive real numbers } x \text{ and } y \text{ such that } x^2 + y^2 + \frac{1}{x^2 + 2x} + \frac{1}{y^2 + 2y} = -2

positive_text: \left( \frac{x+y}{z^2} + \frac{y+z}{x^2} + \frac{z+x}{y^2} \right) \cdot \left( \frac{x^2}{y+z} + \frac{y^2}{z+x} + \frac{z^2}{x+y} \right) \ge 3 + \frac{x+y}{z} + \frac{y+z}{x} + \frac{z+x}{y}

negatives.text: \left( \frac{a+b}{c^2} + \frac{b+c}{a^2} + \frac{c+a}{b^2} \right) \cdot \left( \frac{a^2}{b+c} + \frac{b^2}{c+a} + \frac{c^2}{a+b} \right) \le 3 + \frac{a+b}{c} + \frac{b+c}{a} + \frac{c+a}{b}
\left( \frac{a+b}{c^2} + \frac{b+c}{a^2} + \frac{c+a}{b^2} \right) \cdot \left( \frac{a^2}{b+c} + \frac{b^2}{c+a} + \frac{c^2}{a+b} \right) \ge 3 + \frac{a+b}{c^2} + \frac{b+c}{a^2} + \frac{c+a}{b^2}
\left( \frac{a+b}{c^2} + \frac{b+c}{a^2} + \frac{c+a}{b^2} \right) + \left( \frac{a^2}{b+c} + \frac{b^2}{c+a} + \frac{c^2}{a+b} \right) \ge 3 + \frac{a+b}{c} + \frac{b+c}{a} + \frac{c+a}{b}

positive_text: \text{Suppose } |a+b| + |a-b| = 1. \text{ Determine the minimum and maximum values of } a^2 - 6a + b^2 - 6b.

negatives.text: \text{Given } |x+y| + |x-y| = 1, \text{ find the minimum and maximum of } x^2 - 6x + y^2 + 6y.
\text{Suppose } |x+y| + |x-y| = 1, \text{ find the minimum and maximum of } x^2 - 6x + y^2 - 6y + 100.
\text{Given } |x+y| + |x-y| = 2, \text{ find the minimum and maximum of } x^2 - 6x + y^2 - 6y.

positive_text: Side $CB$ of the parallelogram $ABCD$ is extended beyond $C$ to a point $K$ such that triangle $KDC$ is isosceles with base $CK$. Side $DC$ is extended beyond $C$ to a point $L$ such that triangle $BCL$ is isosceles with base $CL$. The angle bisectors of $\angle LBC$ and $\angle KDC$ intersect at point $Q$. If $\angle BQD = \alpha$ and $KL = a$, find the radius of the circle circumscribed about triangle $ALK$.

negatives.text: Side $BC$ of the parallelogram $ABCD$ is extended beyond $C$ to point $K$ such that triangle $CDK$ is isosceles with base $CK$. Side $DC$ is extended beyond $C$ to point $L$ such that triangle $CBL$ is isosceles with base $CL$. The angle bisectors of $\angle LBC$ and $\angle CDK$ intersect at point $Q$. If $\angle BQD = \alpha$ and $KL = a$, find the radius of the circle inscribed in triangle $ALK$.

Side $BC$ of the parallelogram $ABCD$ is extended beyond $C$ to point $K$ such that triangle $CDK$ is isosceles with base $CK$. Side $DC$ is extended beyond $C$ to point $L$ such that triangle $CBL$ is isosceles with base $CL$. The angle bisectors of $\angle LBC$ and $\angle CDK$ intersect at point $Q$. If $\angle BQD = \alpha$ and $KL = a$, find the area of triangle $ALK$.

positive_text: For which value of $\beta$ does the equation $|x - \frac{1}{2}| + |x - \sin \beta| = \cos 3\beta$ have exactly one solution? Determine that solution.

negatives.text: What should be the value of the parameter $\alpha$ in order that equation $|x - \frac{1}{2}| + |x - \sin \alpha| = \sin 3\alpha$ has a single solution? Find this solution.
What should be the value of the parameter $\alpha$ in order that equation $|x - \frac{1}{2}| + |x - \sin \alpha| = -\cos 3\alpha$ has a single solution? Find this solution.
What should be the value of the parameter $\alpha$ in order that equation $|x - \frac{1}{2}| + |x - \sin \alpha| = \cos 3\alpha + 1$ has a single solution? Find this solution.

positive_text: Let $\{f_n\}$ be a sequence with $f_1 = 1$, $f_2 = 2$, and $f_{n+2} = f_{n+1} + f_n$ for any positive integer $n$. Determine the maximum number of consecutive terms of $\{f_n\}$ that can also form an increasing arithmetic progression.

negatives.text: Let $\{f_n\}$ be a sequence with $f_1 = 1$, $f_2 = 2$, and $f_{n+2} = f_{n+1} - f_n$ for any positive integer $n$. What is the maximum number of consecutive terms of $\{f_n\}$ that can also form an increasing arithmetic progression?

Let $\{f_n\}$ be a sequence with $f_1 = 1$, $f_2 = 2$, and $f_{n+2} = f_{n+1} + f_n$ for any positive integer $n$. What is the maximum number of terms of $\{f_n\}$ that can be in a decreasing arithmetic progression?

Let $\{f_n\}$ be a sequence with $f_1 = 1$, $f_2 = 2$, and $f_{n+2} = f_{n+1} + f_n^2$ for any positive integer $n$. What is the maximum number of consecutive terms of $\{f_n\}$ that can also form an increasing arithmetic progression?

positive_text: Let $a = x - y$, $b = y - z$, and $c = z - x$. If $\frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{b} + \frac{1}{c} = \frac{3}{2}$, find a possible value of $\frac{1}{a^2} + \frac{1}{b^2} + \frac{1}{c^2}$.

negatives.text: Suppose $\frac{1}{(x-y)} + \frac{1}{(y-z)} + \frac{1}{(z-x)} = \frac{3}{2}$ and $\frac{1}{(x-y)^2} + \frac{1}{(y-z)^2} + \frac{1}{(z-x)^2} = k$. What is the value of $\frac{1}{(x-y)^3} + \frac{1}{(y-z)^3} + \frac{1}{(z-x)^3}$ in terms of $k$?

Suppose $\frac{1}{x-y} + \frac{1}{y-z} + \frac{1}{z-x} = \frac{3}{2}$ and $\frac{1}{(x-y)^2} + \frac{1}{(y-z)^2} + \frac{1}{(z-x)^2} = k$. What is the value of $\frac{1}{x-y} + \frac{1}{y-z} + \frac{1}{z-x} + \frac{1}{(x-y)^2} + \frac{1}{(y-z)^2} + \frac{1}{(z-x)^2}$ in terms of $k$?

positive_text: Let $\sigma(k)$ represent the sum of the divisors of a positive integer $k$, and let $\phi(k)$ be the count of positive integers less than $k$ that are relatively prime to $k$. Demonstrate that there are infinitely many positive integers $n$ such that $\phi(\sigma(n)) > n$.

negatives.text: Let $\sigma(k)$ be the sum of the divisors of a positive integer $k$, and $\phi(k)$ the count of positive integers less than $k$ that are relatively prime to $k$. Prove that there are infinitely many positive integers $n$ for which $\phi(\sigma(n)) < n$.

Define $\sigma(k)$ as the sum of the divisors of a positive integer $k$, and $\phi(k)$ as the count of positive integers less than $k$ that are relatively prime to $k$. Prove that there are infinitely many positive integers $n$ such that $\sigma(\phi(n)) > n$.

Let $\sigma(k)$ denote the sum of the divisors of a positive integer $k$, and $\phi(k)$ the number of positive integers less than $k$ that are relatively prime to $k$. Prove that there are infinitely many positive integers $n$ for which $\phi(\sigma(n)) = n$.

positive_text:
Find all real-coefficient polynomials $P(x)$ such that for all distinct positive integers $a, b, c, d$ with $a^2 + b^2 + c^2 = 2d^2$ and $\gcd(a, b, c, d) = 1$, the identity
$$
2P^2(d) + 2P(ab + bc + ca) = P^2(a + b + c)
$$
holds.

negatives.text:
Find all real-coefficient polynomials $P(x)$ such that for all distinct positive integers $x, y, z, t$ with $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 2t^2$ and $\gcd(x, y, z, t) = 1$, the identity
$$
2P^2(t) - 2P(xy + yz + zx) = P^2(x + y + z)
$$
holds.

Find all real-coefficient polynomials $P(x)$ such that for all distinct positive integers $x, y, z, t$ with $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 2t^2$ and $\gcd(x, y, z, t) = 1$, the identity
$$
2P^2(t) + 2P(x + y + z) = P^2(xy + yz + zx)
$$
holds.

positive_text: \frac{OA^2}{CB} + \frac{OB^2}{AC} + \frac{OC^2}{BA} \ge \frac{OA + OB + OC}{\sqrt{3}} \text{ where } O \text{ is a point inside triangle } ABC \text{ such that } \angle AOB = \angle BOC = \angle COA = 120^\circ.

negatives.text: \frac{AO^2}{BC} + \frac{BO^2}{CA} + \frac{CO^2}{AB} \le \frac{AO + BO + CO}{\sqrt{3}} \text{ where } O \text{ is the point inside triangle } ABC \text{ such that } \angle AOB = \angle BOC = \angle COA = 120^\circ.

\frac{AO^3}{BC} + \frac{BO^3}{CA} + \frac{CO^3}{AB} \ge \frac{AO + BO + CO}{\sqrt{3}} \text{ where } O \text{ is the point inside triangle } ABC \text{ such that } \angle AOB = \angle BOC = \angle COA = 120^\circ.

\frac{AO^2}{BC} + \frac{BO^2}{CA} + \frac{CO^2}{AB} \ge \frac{AO + BO + CO}{2} \text{ where } O \text{ is the point inside triangle } ABC \text{ such that } \angle AOB = \angle BOC = \angle COA = 120^\circ.

positive_text: Determine the number of positive integer pairs $(n, m)$ such that $m = \frac{(2^k)!}{2^n}$.

negatives.text: Find the number of pairs of positive integer numbers $(n, m)$, satisfying $(2^k)! = 2^n + m$.
Find the number of pairs of positive integer numbers $(n, m)$, satisfying $(2^k)! = 2^n m^2$.
Find the number of pairs of positive integer numbers $(n, m)$, satisfying $(2^k)! = 2^n m$ with $n > k$.

positive_text: Determine all positive integers $ n $ such that for any polynomial $ f(x) $ with real coefficients, there exist polynomials $ a_1(x), a_2(x),..., a_n(x) $ and $ b_1(x), b_2(x),..., b_n(x) $ satisfying $ f(x) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} (a_i^2(x) + b_i^3(x)) $.

negatives.text: Find all positive integers $ n $ such that for every polynomial $ g(x) $ with real coefficients there exist such polynomials $ p_1(x), p_2(x),..., p_n(x) $ and $ q_1(x), q_2(x),..., q_n(x) $ that $ g(x) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} (p_i^2(x) - q_i^3(x)) $.

Determine all positive integers $ n $ such that for any polynomial $ g(x) $ with real coefficients there exist such polynomials $ p_1(x), p_2(x),..., p_n(x) $ and $ q_1(x), q_2(x),..., q_n(x) $ that $ g(x) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} (p_i^2(x) + q_i^2(x)) $.

Find all positive integers $ n $ such that for every polynomial $ g(x) $ with real coefficients there exist such polynomials $ p_1(x), p_2(x),..., p_n(x) $ and $ q_1(x), q_2(x),..., q_n(x) $ that $ g(x) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} (p_i^2(x) + q_i^3(x)) $ and all $ p_i(x) $ are degree less than 3.

positive_text: Let $x, y, z$ be integers such that $xy + yz + zx = 1$. Prove that the expression $(1 + x^2)(1 + y^2)(1 + z^2)$ is a perfect square of a natural number.

negatives.text: Integers $a, b, c$ satisfy $ab + bc + ca = 1$. Prove that $(1 - a^2)(1 - b^2)(1 - c^2)$ is a perfect square of some natural number.
Integers $a, b, c$ satisfy $ab + bc + ca = 1$. Prove that $(1 + a^2)(1 + b^2)(1 + c^2)$ is a perfect cube of some natural number.
Integers $a, b, c$ satisfy $ab + bc + ca = 2$. Prove that $(1 + a^2)(1 + b^2)(1 + c^2)$ is a perfect square of some natural number.

positive_text: \text{Graph the set of all points } (x, y) \text{ such that } \frac{x}{|x|} + \frac{|y|}{y} - 2y = 0.

negatives.text: \text{Draw the graphic of the equation: } \frac{x}{|x|} + \frac{|y|}{y} = -2y.
\text{Draw the graphic of the equation: } \frac{x}{|x|} + \frac{|y|}{y} = y.
\text{Draw the graphic of the equation: } \frac{x}{|x|} + \frac{|y|}{y} = 2|x|.

positive_text:
Let $x$, $y$, $z$ be nonnegative real numbers such that $x + y + z = 1$. Prove that
$$
(x - 1)^2 + (y - 1)^2 + (z - 1)^2 \geq 6\sqrt{xyz}.
$$

positive_text: Let $ H $ be the orthocenter of triangle $ ABC $, and let $ O_A, O_B, O_C $ be the circumcenters of triangles $ HBC, HAC, HAB $, respectively. If $ O_P $ is the circumcenter of triangle $ O_A O_B O_C $, prove that $ O_P = H $.

positive_text: Let triangle $ABC$ be acute-angled. Points $P$ and $Q$ lie on the perpendicular bisectors of $AB$ and $BC$ respectively. negatives.text: Let triangle $ABC$ be acute-angled. Points $P$ and $Q$ lie on the perpendicular bisectors of $AB$ and $BC$ respectively. positive_text:
Let triangle $ABC$ contain a point $P$ such that the incenter of triangle $I_A I_B I_C$, where $I_A$, $I_B$, $I_C$ are the incenters of triangles $PBC$, $PAC$, and $PAB$ respectively, coincides with $P$. Prove the identities:
$$
AP - BP = AC - BC, \quad BP - CP = BA - CA, \quad CP - AP = CB - AB.
$$

negatives.text:
Point $P$ lies inside triangle $ABC$. Let $I_A$, $I_B$, $I_C$ be incenters of triangles $PBC$, $PAC$, $PAB$ respectively. Let $I_P$ denote the incenter of triangle $I_A I_B I_C$. Prove that for point $P$ which satisfies the condition $I_P = P$, the following equalities hold:

Point $P$ lies inside triangle $ABC$. Let $I_A$, $I_B$, $I_C$ be incenters of triangles $PBC$, $PAC$, $PAB$ respectively. Let $I_P$ denote the incenter of triangle $I_A I_B I_C$. Prove that for point $P$ which satisfies the condition $I_P = P$, the following equalities hold:

$$
AP - BP = BC - AC, \quad BP - CP = CA - BA, \quad CP - AP = AB - CB.
$$

positive_text: Show that for every positive integer $k$, there exist infinitely many natural numbers $x, y, z$ satisfying $x^k + 2010y^k = z^{k+1}$.

negatives.text: Prove that for all positive integers $n$, the equation $a^n - 2010b^n = c^{n+1}$ has infinitely many natural solutions $a, b, c$.

Prove that for all positive integers $n$, the equation $a^{n+1} + 2010b^{n+1} = c^{n+1}$ has infinitely many natural solutions $a, b, c$.

positive_text: \text{Let } a, b, c \in (0, 1]. \text{ Prove that: } \frac{a}{2+ab+bc} + \frac{b}{2+bc+ca} + \frac{c}{2+ca+ab} \le \frac{a+b+c}{a+b+c+abc}

negatives.text: \text{Let } x, y, z \in (0, 1]. \text{ Prove that: } \frac{x}{2+xy+yz} + \frac{y}{2+yz+zx} + \frac{z}{2+zx+xy} \ge \frac{x+y+z}{x+y+z+xyz}

positive_text: Let $\omega$ be the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$. The angle bisector of $\angle BAC$ intersects $BC$ at $L$ and the circumcircle again at $D$. A segment $DK$ is drawn perpendicular to $AC$, meeting it at $M$. Given that $\frac{BL}{LC} = \frac{1}{2}$, determine the value of $\frac{AM}{MC}$.

negatives.text: Let $\omega$ be the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$. Chord $AD$ is a bisector of triangle $ABC$ and meets $BC$ at $L$, chord $DK$ is parallel to $AC$ and meets it at $M$. Find the ratio $\frac{AM}{MC}$, if $\frac{BL}{LC} = \frac{1}{2}$.

Let $\omega$ be the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$. Chord $AD$ is a bisector of triangle $ABC$ and meets $BC$ at $L$, chord $DK$ is perpendicular to $AC$ and meets it at $M$. Find the ratio $\frac{AM}{MC}$, if $\frac{BL}{LC} = \frac{2}{1}$.

positive_text: On triangle $ABC$, points $K$ and $M$ lie on $AB$ and $BC$ respectively such that $AK = KM = MC$. Let $N$ be the intersection of $AM$ and $CK$, and let $P$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $N$ to $KM$. Define $Q$ as the point on segment $KM$ such that $MQ = KP$. Show that the incircle of triangle $KMB$ is tangent to segment $KM$ at $Q$.

negatives.text: Points $K$ and $M$ lie on sides $AB$ and $BC$ of triangle $ABC$ such that $AK = KM = MC$. Let $N$ be the intersection of $AM$ and $CK$, and let $P$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $N$ to $KM$. Define $Q$ as the point on $KM$ such that $MQ = 2KP$. Prove that the incircle of triangle $KMB$ is tangent to segment $KM$ at $Q$.

positive_text:
Let $ \triangle ABC $ have vertex $ A $ and let $ h $ be the height from $ A $ to $ BC $. Given $ \alpha = \angle BAC $, prove that:
$$
AB + AC \ge BC \cdot \cos \alpha + 2h \sin \alpha.
$$
When does equality occur?

negatives.text:
Let $ h $ be the altitude of triangle $ ABC $ from vertex $ A $ and $ \alpha = \angle BAC $. Prove that the following inequality holds:

AB + AC \le BC \cdot \cos \alpha + 2h \sin \alpha.
$$

Let $ h $ be the altitude of triangle $ ABC $ from vertex $ A $ and $ \alpha = \angle BAC $. Prove that the following inequality holds:
$$
AB + AC \ge BC \cdot \cos \alpha + 2h \sin (\alpha / 2).
$$
In what triangles does equality hold?

positive_text: Determine all values of the constant $ b $ such that for every real number $ x $, at least one of the expressions $ x^2 + 2011x + b $ or $ x^2 - 2011x + b $ is greater than zero.

negatives.text: Find all values of parameter $ b $, such that for all $ x $, at least one function $ f_1(x) = x^2 + 2011x + b $ or $ f_2(x) = x^2 - 2011x - b $ is positive.
Find all values of parameter $ b $, such that for all $ x $, both functions $ f_1(x) = x^2 + 2011x + b $ and $ f_2(x) = x^2 - 2011x + b $ are positive.
Find all values of parameter $ b $, such that for all $ x $, at least one function $ f_1(x) = x^2 + 2011x + b $ or $ f_2(x) = x^2 - 2011x + b $ is non-negative.

positive_text: Find all real solutions $x$ such that $$\cos \pi x = \left\lfloor \frac{x}{2} - \left\lfloor \frac{x}{2} \right\rfloor - \frac{1}{2} \right\rfloor.$$

negatives.text: Solve the equation: $$\sin \pi x = \left[ \frac{x}{2} - \left[ \frac{x}{2} \right] - \frac{1}{2} \right].$$

positive_text:
Determine all non-negative real-valued functions $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfying the identity:
$$
f(2a) = f(a+b)f(b-a) + f(a-b)f(-a-b)
$$
for all real numbers $a, b$.

negatives.text:

$$
for all real $x, y$, and $f(x) \ge 0$ for all $x$.

positive_text: Let $ABC$ be a triangle inscribed in a circle. The tangents at $A$ and $B$ intersect at point $T$. A line through $T$ parallel to $AC$ meets $BC$ at $D$. Show that triangle $ADC$ is isosceles.

negatives.text: Triangle $ABC$ is inscribed in a circle. Tangents at points $A$ and $B$ meet at point $T$. The line through $T$ perpendicular to $AC$ intersects $BC$ at point $D$. Prove that $AD = CD$.

positive_text: In triangle $ABC$, let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$, and let $N$ lie on $AB$ such that $AN : NB = 1 : 2$. If $\angle BAC = \angle CMN$, determine $\frac{AC}{BC}$.

positive_text:

$$
for all real numbers $ a $ and $ b $. If $ f(2011) = 2012 $, determine $ f(2012) $.

positive_text: Let $O$ be the circumcenter of an acute scalene triangle $ABC$. Let $BO$ intersect $AC$ at $K$, and $CO$ intersect $AB$ at $N$. Prove that for $n \geq 1$, the last $n+2$ digits of $11^{10^{n}}$ are $7000 \ldots 0001$, with $n$ zeros between the 7 and the final 1.

positive_text: Show that there is a polynomial $g(a, b, c)$ such that the quantities $|a|, |b|$, and $|c|$ satisfy the triangle inequality if and only if $g(a, b, c) > 0$.

negatives.text: Prove that there exists a polynomial $f(x, y, z)$ with the following property: the numbers $|x|, |y|$, and $|z|$ are the sides of a degenerate triangle if and only if $f(x, y, z) > 0$.
Prove that there exists a polynomial $f(x, y, z)$ with the following property: the numbers $|x|, |y|$, and $|z|$ are the sides of a triangle if and only if $f(x, y, z) < 0$.
Prove that there exists a polynomial $f(x, y, z)$ with the following property: the numbers $x^2, y^2$, and $z^2$ are the sides of a triangle if and only if $f(x, y, z) > 0$.

positive_text: Given that $x, y, z, w$ are positive real numbers with $\frac{5 x+y}{5 z+w}=\frac{6 x+y}{6 z+w}$ and $\frac{7 x+y}{7 z+w}=9$, find $\frac{9 x+y}{9 z+w}$.

negatives.text: If $a, b, c, d$ are positive real numbers such that $\frac{5 a-b}{5 c-d}=\frac{6 a-b}{6 c-d}$ and $\frac{7 a-b}{7 c-d}=9$, calculate $\frac{9 a-b}{9 c-d}$.
If $a, b, c, d$ are positive real numbers such that $\frac{5 a+b}{5 c+d}=\frac{6 a+b}{6 c+d}$ and $\frac{7 a+b}{7 c+d} \leq 9$, find the maximum possible value of $\frac{9 a+b}{9 c+d}$.
If $a, b, c, d$ are positive real numbers such that $\frac{5 a+b}{5 c+d}+\frac{6 a+b}{6 c+d}=\frac{7 a+b}{7 c+d}$ and $\frac{7 a+b}{7 c+d}=9$, calculate $\frac{9 a+b}{9 c+d}$.

positive_text: Let $A$ be an $n \times n$ matrix with entries $a_{i j} = \frac{1}{i + j - 1}$. Suppose one entry is selected from each row and each column. Prove that the sum of the selected entries is at least $1$.

negatives.text: Let $A$ be an $n \times n$ matrix with entries $a_{i j} = \frac{1}{i - j + 1}$. Suppose one entry is selected from each row and each column. Prove that the sum of the selected entries is at least $1$.

Let $A$ be an $n \times n$ matrix with entries $a_{i j} = \frac{1}{(i + j - 1)^2}$. Suppose one entry is selected from each row and each column. Prove that the sum of the selected entries is at least $1$.

Let $A$ be an $n \times n$ matrix with entries $a_{i j} = \frac{1}{i + j - 1}$. Suppose one entry is selected from each row and each column. Prove that the product of the selected entries is at least $1$.

positive_text: \text{Let } x \text{ and } y \text{ be positive real numbers. Prove that } \sqrt{x^{2}-x y+y^{2}} \geq \frac{x+y}{2}

negatives.text: \text{Let } a \text{ and } b \text{ be positive real numbers. Prove that } \sqrt{a^{2}+a b+b^{2}} \geq \frac{a+b}{2}
\text{Let } a \text{ and } b \text{ be positive real numbers. Prove that } \sqrt{a^{2}-a b+b^{2}} \geq \frac{a-b}{2}
\text{Let } a \text{ and } b \text{ be positive real numbers. Prove that } \sqrt{a^{2}-a b+b^{2}} \leq \frac{a+b}{2}

positive_text:
Let $ABC$ be an isosceles right triangle with $\angle C = 90^\circ$. Let $X$ be a point on segment $AC$, and let $Y$ and $Z$ be the projections of $A$ and $C$ onto the line $BX$. Prove that
$$
BZ = AY + YZ
$$

negatives.text:
Let $ABC$ be an isosceles right triangle with $\angle C = 90^\circ$. Let $X$ be a point on segment $AC$, and let $Y$ and $Z$ be the feet of the perpendiculars from $A$ and $B$ to the line $CX$. Prove that
$$
BZ = YZ + AY
$$

Let $ABC$ be an isosceles right triangle with $\angle C = 90^\circ$. Let $X$ be a point on segment $AC$, and let $Y$ and $Z$ be the feet of the perpendiculars from $A$ and $C$ to the line $BX$. Prove that
$$
BZ = YZ - AY
$$

Let $ABC$ be an isosceles right triangle with $\angle C = 90^\circ$. Let $X$ be a point on segment $AC$, and let $Y$ and $Z$ be the feet of the perpendiculars from $A$ and $C$ to the line $BX$. Prove that
$$
BZ^2 = YZ^2 + AY^2
$$

positive_text: Prove that every integer $n$ satisfying $n \geq 17$ allows a square to be partitioned into $n$ smaller squares.

negatives.text: Show that for each $n \geq 17$ one can cut a square into $n$ smaller rectangles.
Show that for each $n \geq 17$ one can cut a square into $n$ smaller squares of equal area.
Show that for each $n \geq 17$ one can cut a square into $n$ smaller squares with no two of the same size.

positive_text:
Show that the value of
$$
A=\sqrt{4-2 \sqrt{3}}-\frac{1+\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}-1}
$$
is an integer.

negatives.text:
Prove that
$$
A=\sqrt{4+2 \sqrt{3}}-\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{\sqrt{3}-1}
$$
is an integer.

Prove that
$$
A=\sqrt{4-2 \sqrt{3}}+\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{\sqrt{3}-1}
$$
is an integer.

$$
A=\sqrt{4-2 \sqrt{3}}-\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{\sqrt{3}+1}
$$
is an integer.

positive_text: Let square $ABCD$ have side length $1$. A dilation centered at $A$ transforms it into square $AB' C' D'$. Given that the length of segment $BC'$ is $29$, find the area of triangle $BDC'$.

negatives.text: Square $ABCD$ has side length $1$. A dilation is performed about point $A$, creating square $AB' C' D'$. If $B C' = 29$, determine the area of triangle $BC D'$.
Square $ABCD$ has side length $1$. A dilation is performed about point $A$, creating square $AB' C' D'$. If $B C' = 29$, determine the area of triangle $BD C$.
Square $ABCD$ has side length $1$. A dilation is performed about point $A$, creating square $AB' C' D'$. If $B C' = 29$, determine the area of triangle $A B C'$.

positive_text: Prove that for all integers $k \geq 3$, there exist $k$ distinct positive integers $d_1, d_2, \ldots, d_k$ such that $\frac{1}{d_1} + \frac{1}{d_2} + \cdots + \frac{1}{d_k} = 1$.

negatives.text: For any positive integer $n \geq 3$, show that you can write $2$ as a sum of $n$ fractions with numerator $1$ and different denominators.
For any positive integer $n \geq 3$, show that you can write $1$ as a product of $n$ fractions with numerator $1$ and different denominators.
For any positive integer $n \geq 3$, show that you can write $1$ as a sum of $n$ fractions with distinct numerators and denominator $1$.

positive_text: Determine all integer solutions $(a, b)$ to the equation $a^{2} + a b = b^{2}$.

negatives.text: Find all pairs of integers $(x, y)$ for which $x^{2} - x y = y^{2}$.
Find all pairs of integers $(x, y)$ for which $x^{2} + x y = y^{3}$.
Find all pairs of integers $(x, y)$ for which $x^{2} + x y = y^{2} + 1$.

positive_text: Suppose $\frac{x}{y}$ and $\frac{u}{v}$ are approximately equal in the sense that $\frac{x}{y} - \frac{u}{v} = \frac{1}{yv}$, where $x, y, u, v$ are positive integers. Prove that there exists a positive integer $k$ such that adding or subtracting 1 to each of $kx, ky, ku, kv$ yields two equal fractions.

negatives.text: Suppose $\frac{a}{b} - \frac{c}{d} = \frac{1}{bd}$. Prove that we can multiply each of the four numbers by the same positive integer and then add or subtract 2 from each of them to obtain equal fractions.
Suppose $\frac{a}{b} + \frac{c}{d} = \frac{1}{bd}$. Prove that we can multiply the four numbers by the same positive integer and then add or subtract 1 from each of them to obtain equal fractions.
Suppose $\frac{a}{b} - \frac{c}{d} = \frac{1}{b^2}$. Prove that we can multiply the four numbers by the same positive integer and then add or subtract 1 from each of them to obtain equal fractions.

positive_text: Suppose $x$, $y$, and $z$ are positive real numbers satisfying $x + 2y + 4z = 8$. What is the maximum value of $xyz$?

negatives.text: If $a$, $b$, and $c$ are positive real numbers with $2a + 4b + 8c = 16$, what is the smallest possible value of $abc$?
If $a$, $b$, and $c$ are positive real numbers with $2a^2 + 4b^2 + 8c^2 = 16$, what is the largest possible value of $abc$?
If $a$, $b$, and $c$ are positive real numbers with $2a + 4b + 8c = 16$, what is the largest possible value of $a + b + c$?

positive_text: Given triangles $PQR$ and $P'Q'R'$ with $\angle P = \angle P'$, $PQ = P'Q'$, and $QR = Q'R'$, and with $\angle R = 90^\circ$, show that the triangles are congruent.

negatives.text: Suppose that $ABC$ and $A'B'C'$ are two triangles such that $\angle A = \angle A'$, $AB = A'B'$, and $AC = A'C'$. Suppose also that $\angle C = 90^\circ$. Prove that triangles $ABC$ and $A'B'C'$ are congruent.

Suppose that $ABC$ and $A'B'C'$ are two triangles such that $\angle A = \angle A'$, $AB = A'B'$, and $BC = B'C'$. Suppose also that $\angle B = 90^\circ$. Prove that triangles $ABC$ and $A'B'C'$ are congruent.

positive_text:
Let $a$ and $b$ be positive real numbers such that $a, b < 1$. Show that
$$
\frac{1}{1-a^{2}} + \frac{1}{1-b^{2}} \geq \frac{2}{1-ab}
$$

negatives.text:
If $x$ and $y$ are positive numbers less than $1$, prove that
$$
\frac{1}{1-x^{2}} + \frac{1}{1-y^{2}} < \frac{2}{1-xy}
$$

Let $x$ and $y$ be positive numbers less than $1$. Prove that
$$
\frac{1}{1-x^{2}} + \frac{1}{1-y^{2}} \geq \frac{2}{1-(x+y)}
$$

Let $x$ and $y$ be positive real numbers less than $1$. Prove that
$$
\frac{1}{1-x} + \frac{1}{1-y} \geq \frac{2}{1-xy}
$$

positive_text: Let triangle $ABC$ have a right angle at $B$. Let $k$ be a circle centered on $BC$ that is tangent to side $AC$. Let $T$ be the point where $k$ touches the tangent from $A$ other than $AC$. If $B'$ is the midpoint of $AC$ and $M$ is the intersection of $BB'$ and $AT$, show that $MB = MT$.

negatives.text: Let triangle $ABC$ have a right angle at $B$. Let $k$ be a circle centered on $BC$ that is tangent to side $AC$. Let $T$ be the point where $k$ touches the tangent from $A$ other than $AC$. If $B'$ is the midpoint of $AB$ and $M$ is the intersection of $BB'$ and $AT$, prove that $MB = MT$.

Let triangle $ABC$ have a right angle at $B$. Let $k$ be a circle centered on $BC$ that is tangent to side $AC$. Let $T$ be the point where $k$ touches the tangent from $C$ other than $AC$. If $B'$ is the midpoint of $AC$ and $M$ is the intersection of $BB'$ and $CT$, prove that $MB = MT$.

positive_text:
Let $Q(x)$ be a nonzero polynomial with real coefficients such that
$$
Q(x) = Q(0) + Q(1) x + Q(2) x^{2}
$$
for all $x$. Determine all roots of $Q(x)$.

negatives.text:
Let $P(x)$ be a nonzero polynomial with real coefficients such that
$$
P(x) = P(0) + P(1) x + P(2) x^{3}
$$
holds for all $x$. What are the roots of $P(x)$?

Let $P(x)$ be a nonzero polynomial with real coefficients such that
$$
P(x) = P(0) + P(1) x + P(2) x^{2}
$$
holds for all $x$. What are the coefficients of $P(x)$?

Let $P(x)$ be a nonzero polynomial with real coefficients such that
$$
P(x) = P(0) + P(1) x + P(2) x^{2}
$$
for all $x$. Find the degree of $P(x)$.

positive_text: Let $n > 3$ be an integer with $n \not\equiv 0 \pmod{3}$. Players $A$ and $B$ play a game on an $n \times n$ chocolate board. Player $A$ removes one square, and then player $B$ attempts to tile the remaining board with domino-like tiles of size $3 \times 1$ or $1 \times 3$. If player $B$ succeeds, they win; otherwise, player $A$ wins. Identify the player with a winning strategy and describe it.

negatives.text: Let $n > 3$ be an integer not divisible by $3$. Players $A$ and $B$ play a game on an $n \times n$ chocolate board. Player $A$ removes one square, and then player $B$ attempts to tile the remaining board with $2 \times 1$ dominoes. If player $B$ succeeds, they win; otherwise, player $A$ wins. Determine the winner with a winning strategy.

Let $n > 3$ be an integer not divisible by $3$. Players $A$ and $B$ play a game on an $n \times n$ chocolate board. Player $A$ removes one square, and then player $B$ attempts to tile the remaining board with $3 \times 1$ and $1 \times 3$ rectangles, but now the board is wrapped on a torus (i.e., the top and bottom rows are connected and the left and right columns are connected). If player $B$ succeeds, they win; otherwise, player $A$ wins. Determine the winner with a winning strategy.

positive_text: \text{a. Show that for all real numbers } a \text{ and } b,\quad a^{2}-2 b^{2}=-\left[(a+2 b)^{2}-2(a+b)^{2}\right].\n\text{b. Determine how many positive integer solutions the equation } a^{2}-2 b^{2}=1 \text{ has.}\n\text{c. Determine how many positive integer solutions the equation } a^{2}-2 b^{2}=5 \text{ has.}

negatives.text: \text{a. Prove that for all real numbers } x \text{ and } y,\quad x^{2}+2 y^{2}=-\left[(x+2 y)^{2}-2(x+y)^{2}\right].\n\text{b. How many positive integer solutions does the equation } x^{2}+2 y^{2}=1 \text{ have?}\n\text{c. How many positive integer solutions does the equation } x^{2}+2 y^{2}=5 \text{ have?}

positive_text: Let $PQRS$ be a square in the coordinate plane such that $P$ lies on the $x$-axis and $R$ lies on the $y$-axis. Prove that one of the points $Q$ or $S$ lies on the line $y = x$.

negatives.text: Let $ABCD$ be a square in the coordinate plane such that $A$ is on the $x$-axis and $C$ is on the $y$-axis. Prove that one of the vertices $B$ and $D$ lies on the line $y = -x$.
Let $ABCD$ be a rectangle in the coordinate plane such that $A$ is on the $x$-axis and $C$ is on the $y$-axis. Prove that one of the vertices $B$ and $D$ lies on the line $y = x$.
Let $ABCD$ be a square in the coordinate plane such that $A$ is at the origin and $C$ is on the $y$-axis. Prove that one of the vertices $B$ and $D$ lies on the line $y = x$.

positive_text: Let $x$ be a real number satisfying $x \geq 4$. Show that $$ \sqrt{x} - \sqrt{x - 1} \geq \frac{1}{x}. $$

negatives.text: If $x \geq 4$ is a real number, prove that $$ \sqrt{x} - \sqrt{x - 1} \geq \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}. $$

If $x \geq 4$ is a real number, prove that $$ \sqrt{x} + \sqrt{x - 1} \geq \frac{1}{x}. $$

positive_text: Let $n$ be an integer greater than $2$. Positive real numbers $a$ and $b$ satisfy $a^{n} = a + 1$ and $b^{n+1} = b^{3} + 1$. Show that $a < b$.

negatives.text: Let $n$ be an integer greater than $2$. Positive real numbers $x$ and $y$ satisfy $x^{n} = x - 1$ and $y^{n+1} = y^{3} + 1$. Prove that $x < y$.

positive_text:
Determine all functions $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ such that
$$
 f(a+b) = f(a-b) + 4ab
$$
for all real numbers $a$ and $b$.

negatives.text:
Find all functions $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ such that
$$
 f(x+y) = f(x-y) - 4xy
$$
for all real numbers $x$ and $y$.

Find all functions $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ such that
$$
 f(x+y) = f(x-y) + 4x^2
$$
for all real numbers $x$ and $y$.

$$

$$

positive_text: Let $g(n)$ denote the number of digits in the base-10 representation of $n$. Show that $$ g\left(2^{n}\right)+g\left(5^{n}\right)=n+1 $$

negatives.text: Let $f(n)$ be the number of digits of a positive integer $n$ (in base 10). Prove that $$ f\left(2^{n}+5^{n}\right)=n+1 $$

Let $f(n)$ be the number of digits of a positive integer $n$ (in base 10). Prove that $$ f\left(2^{n}\right)+f\left(3^{n}\right)=n+1 $$

positive_text: Find a non-trivial polynomial $Q(p, q, r)$ such that $Q(x^3, y^3, z^3) = 0$ for all real numbers $x, y, z$ with $x + y = z$.

negatives.text: Find a non-zero polynomial $P(x, y, z)$ such that $P(a, b, c)=0$ for every three real numbers that satisfy $\sqrt[3]{a} + \sqrt[3]{b} + \sqrt[3]{c} = 0$.
Find a non-zero polynomial $P(x, y, z)$ such that $P(a, b, c)=0$ for every three real numbers that satisfy $\sqrt{a} + \sqrt{b} = \sqrt{c}$.

positive_text: Determine the number of real solutions to the equation $x^{2} - \arctan x = 1.6$, where the domain of $\arctan x$ is $-\frac{\pi}{2} < \arctan x < \frac{\pi}{2}$.

negatives.text: How many roots does $\arctan x = x^{2} + 1.6$ have, with the arctan function defined in the range $-\frac{\pi}{2} < \arctan x < \frac{\pi}{2}$?

positive_text: Determine the greatest common divisor of $m^{5}-5 m^{3}+4 m$ for all integers $m$ such that $m \geq 5$.

negatives.text: Find the largest integer that divides $m^{5}+5 m^{3}+4 m$ for all $m \geq 5$.
Find the largest integer that divides $m^{5}-5 m^{3}+4 m^{2}$ for all $m \geq 5$.
Find the largest integer that divides $m^{5}-5 m^{3}+4 m$ for all $m \leq 5$.

positive_text:
In triangle $ABC$, suppose $M$ and $N$ are the midpoints of sides $AB$ and $AC$, respectively. Given that
$$
\frac{\text{length of } CM}{\text{length of } AC} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},
$$
show that
$$
\frac{\text{length of } BN}{\text{length of } AB} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.
$$

negatives.text:
Let $ABC$ be a triangle, and let $M$ and $N$ be the respective midpoints of $AB$ and $AC$. Suppose that
$$
\frac{CM}{AC} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}
$$
Prove that
$$
\frac{BN}{AB} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.
$$

positive_text: Let $k$ be a positive integer. Prove that there exist distinct positive integers $a$, $b$, $c$ such that $$ a^{k-1} + b^k = c^{k+1}. $$

negatives.text: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Prove that there exist distinct positive integers $x$, $y$, $z$ such that $$ x^{n+1} + y^n = z^{n-1}. $$
Let $n$ be a positive integer. Prove that there exist distinct positive integers $x$, $y$, $z$ such that $$ x^{n-1} - y^n = z^{n+1}. $$
Let $n$ be a positive integer. Prove that there exist distinct positive integers $x$, $y$, $z$ such that $$ x^{n} + y^{n} = z^{n+1}. $$

positive_text:
Define a number to be 1-rich if it satisfies the following:

a. Each digit is among $\{0, 1, 2\}$.

b. Any pair of adjacent digits includes at least one digit equal to $1$.

Determine the number of such $n$-digit 1-rich numbers for $n \geq 2$, ensuring the first digit is not $0$.

negatives.text:
Call a positive integer one-full if it satisfies the following criteria:

a. Every digit is either $0$, $1$, or $2$.

b. Out of every two consecutive digits, at least one of them is a $0$.

For $n \geq 2$, calculate the number of $n$-digit one-full numbers. (Numbers beginning with the digit $0$ are not allowed.)

Call a positive integer one-full if it satisfies the following criteria:

a. Every digit is either $0$, $1$, or $2$.

b. Out of every two consecutive digits, both of them are $1$.

For $n \geq 2$, calculate the number of $n$-digit one-full numbers. (Numbers beginning with the digit $0$ are not allowed.)

Call a positive integer one-full if it satisfies the following criteria:

a. Every digit is either $0$, $1$, or $2$.

b. Out of every three consecutive digits, at least one of them is a $1$.

For $n \geq 2$, calculate the number of $n$-digit one-full numbers. (Numbers beginning with the digit $0$ are not allowed.)

positive_text:
Let $ \omega = e^{\frac{2\pi i}{n}} $, where $ n $ is a positive odd integer. Show that
$$
\sum_{k=1}^{n} \frac{1}{1 + \omega^{k}} = \frac{n}{2}
$$

negatives.text:
Let $ z = \cos \dfrac{2\pi}{n} + i \sin \dfrac{2\pi}{n} $ where $ n $ is a positive odd integer. Prove that
$$
\frac{1}{1-z} + \frac{1}{1-z^{2}} + \frac{1}{1-z^{3}} + \cdots + \frac{1}{1-z^{n}} = \frac{n}{2}
$$

Let $ z = \cos \dfrac{2\pi}{n} + i \sin \dfrac{2\pi}{n} $ where $ n $ is a positive odd integer. Prove that
$$
\frac{1}{1+z^{2}} + \frac{1}{1+z^{4}} + \cdots + \frac{1}{1+z^{2n}} = \frac{n}{2}
$$

Let $ z = \cos \dfrac{\pi}{n} + i \sin \dfrac{\pi}{n} $ where $ n $ is a positive odd integer. Prove that
$$
\frac{1}{1+z} + \frac{1}{1+z^{2}} + \frac{1}{1+z^{3}} + \cdots + \frac{1}{1+z^{n}} = \frac{n}{2}
$$

positive_text: Let triangle $ABC$ have angle bisector $AD$ with $D$ on side $BC$. Let $O$, $O_1$, and $O_2$ be the centers of the circumcircles of triangles $ABC$, $ABD$, and $ADC$, respectively. Show that the distances from $O$ to $O_1$ and $O_2$ are equal.

negatives.text: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AD$ the external angle bisector of $\angle BAC$ meeting $BC$ extended at $D$. Let $O, O_{1}, O_{2}$ be the circumcenters of triangles $ABC$, $ABD$, and $ADC$, respectively. Prove that $OO_{1} = OO_{2}$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle, and let the bisector of $\angle BAC$ meet $BC$ at $D$. Let $O, O_{1}, O_{2}$ be the incenters of triangles $ABC$, $ABD$, and $ADC$, respectively. Prove that $OO_{1} = OO_{2}$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle, and let the bisector of $\angle BAC$ meet $BC$ at $D$. Let $O, O_{1}, O_{2}$ be the circumcenters of triangles $ABC$, $ABD$, and $ADC$, respectively. Prove that $O_{1}O_{2} = OO_{1}$.

positive_text:
Let $p \leq q \leq r \leq s$ be real numbers such that
$$
p+q+r+s=0 \quad \text{ and } \quad \frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}+\frac{1}{r}+\frac{1}{s}=0
$$
Show that $p+s=0$.

negatives.text:
Let $a \leq b \leq c \leq d$ be real numbers such that
$$
a+b+c+d=0 \quad \text{ and } \quad \frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{b}+\frac{1}{c}+\frac{1}{d}=1
$$
Prove that $a+d=0$.

Let $a \leq b \leq c \leq d$ be real numbers such that
$$
a+b+c+d=0 \quad \text{ and } \quad \frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{b}+\frac{1}{c}+\frac{1}{d}=0
$$
Prove that $a+b=0$.

Let $a \leq b \leq c \leq d$ be real numbers such that
$$
a+b+c+d=1 \quad \text{ and } \quad \frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{b}+\frac{1}{c}+\frac{1}{d}=0
$$
Prove that $a+d=0$.

positive_text:
Find all polynomials $ g $ such that
$$
\frac{g(3x)}{g(x)} = \frac{81x - 243}{x - 27}
$$
holds for infinitely many $ x $.

negatives.text:
Find all polynomials $ f $ such that
$$
\frac{f(9 x)}{f(3 x)} = \frac{243 x + 729}{x - 81}
$$
holds for infinitely many $ x $.

Find all polynomials $ f $ such that
$$
\frac{f(9 x)}{f(3 x)} = \frac{243 x - 729}{x + 81}
$$
holds for infinitely many $ x $.

Find all polynomials $ f $ such that
$$
\frac{f(9 x)}{f(3 x)} = \frac{243 x - 729}{(x - 81)^2}
$$
holds for infinitely many $ x $.

positive_text:
Let $a$, $b$, and $c$ be real numbers such that $a b c = 1$. Prove that
$$
a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2} \geq \frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{b} + \frac{1}{c}
$$

negatives.text:
Let $x$, $y$, and $z$ be real numbers such that $x y z = 1$. Prove that
$$
\frac{1}{x^{2}} + \frac{1}{y^{2}} + \frac{1}{z^{2}} \geq x + y + z
$$

Let $x$, $y$, and $z$ be real numbers such that $x y z = 1$. Prove that
$$
\frac{x^{2}}{y} + \frac{y^{2}}{z} + \frac{z^{2}}{x} \geq x + y + z
$$

Let $x$, $y$, and $z$ be real numbers such that $x y z = 1$. Prove that
$$
\frac{1}{x^{2}} + \frac{1}{y^{2}} + \frac{1}{z^{2}} \leq x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}
$$

positive_text: \text{Let } a, b, c, \text{ and } d \text{ be real numbers satisfying the equation } \frac{a-b}{a+b}+\frac{b-c}{b+c}+\frac{c-d}{c+d}+\frac{d-a}{d+a}=0

negatives.text: \text{Let } x, y, z, \text{ and } u \text{ be real numbers satisfying the equation } \frac{x+y}{x-y}+\frac{y+z}{y-z}+\frac{z+u}{z-u}+\frac{u+x}{u-x}=0
\text{Let } x, y, z, \text{ and } u \text{ be real numbers satisfying the equation } \frac{x-y}{x+y}+\frac{y-z}{y+z}+\frac{z-u}{z+u}+\frac{u-x}{u+x}=1
\text{Let } x, y, z, \text{ and } u \text{ be real numbers satisfying the equation } \frac{x^2 - y^2}{x^2 + y^2}+\frac{y^2 - z^2}{y^2 + z^2}+\frac{z^2 - u^2}{z^2 + u^2}+\frac{u^2 - x^2}{u^2 + x^2}=0

positive_text: Show that for all positive integers $n$, there exists an $n$-digit number $N$ consisting only of the digits $1$ and $2$ for which $2^{n} \mid N$.

negatives.text: Prove that for each $n \geq 1$, there is a number $N$ having $n$ digits, each of which is either $1$ or $2$, such that $N$ is divisible by $2^{n} - 1$.
Prove that for each $n \geq 1$, there is a number $N$ having $n$ digits, each of which is either $1$ or $2$, such that $N$ is divisible by $2^{n+1}$.
Prove that for each $n \geq 1$, there is a number $N$ having $n$ digits, each of which is either $1$ or $2$, such that $N$ is divisible by $2^{n}$ and all digits of $N$ are distinct.

positive_text: Let triangle $ABC$ be given, and define point $D$ on the ray $AB$ such that $BD = AB + AC$. Suppose points $K$ and $M$ lie on segments $AB$ and $BC$, respectively, and that the areas of triangles $BDM$ and $BCK$ are equal. Prove that $\angle BKM = \frac{1}{2} \angle CAB$.

negatives.text: Given triangle $ABC$, let $D$ be the point on the ray $BA$ such that $BD = BA - AC$. If $K$ and $M$ are points on the sides $BA$ and $BC$, respectively, such that the areas of triangles $BDM$ and $BCK$ are equal, prove that $\angle BKM = \frac{1}{2} \angle BAC$.

Given triangle $ABC$, let $D$ be the point on the ray $BA$ such that $BD = AB + AC$. Suppose $K$ and $M$ are points on the sides $AB$ and $BC$, respectively, such that the perimeters of triangles $BDM$ and $BCK$ are equal. Prove that $\angle BKM = \frac{1}{2} \angle BAC$.

Let triangle $ABC$ be given, and define point $D$ on the ray $BA$ such that $BD = BA + AC$. If $K$ and $M$ are points on the sides $BA$ and $BC$, respectively, such that the triangles $BDM$ and $BCK$ have the same areas, prove that $\angle KMB = \frac{1}{2} \angle BAC$.

positive_text: Let $\angle ABC$ be an acute angle with an interior ray $BD$ as shown. Laura has an infinite ruler composed of two parallel rays connected by a segment perpendicular to both. The ruler can be aligned so that an edge passes through two selected points or aligns with a segment, ray, or line in the diagram. After placing the ruler, any of its edges may be drawn, and intersections may be marked. Using only the infinite ruler, construct points $P$ on $BA$ and $Q$ on $BC$ such that $BD$ intersects $PQ$ at a point $R$ where $PR = 2(RQ)$. Prove your construction is valid.

negatives.text: Given an acute angle $\angle ABC$ with ray $BD$ inside, Laura is given an infinite ruler as before. Construct points $P$ on $BA$ and $Q$ on $BC$ such that ray $BD$ intersects ray $PQ$ at a point $R$ with $PR = QR$. Prove your construction.
Using the infinite ruler described, construct points $P$ on $BA$ and $Q$ on $BC$ so that $BD$ intersects $PQ$ at a point $R$ with $PR = 3(RQ)$. Prove correctness.

Using the infinite ruler, construct points $P$ on $BA$ and $Q$ on $BC$ such that $BD$ intersects $PQ$ at a point $R$ with $PR = 2(RQ)$. You may not mark or use intersections for construction, only draw edges of the ruler. Prove your construction.

positive_text:
Let $p(x)$ be a degree-2 polynomial. Prove that there exist degree-2 polynomials $q(x)$ and $r(x)$ such that
$$
 p(x) p(x+1) = q(r(x)).
$$

negatives.text:
Let $f(x)$ be a quadratic polynomial. Prove that there exist quadratic polynomials $g(x)$ and $h(x)$ such that
$$
 f(x) + f(x+1) = g(h(x)).
$$

Let $f(x)$ be a quadratic polynomial. Prove that there exist quadratic polynomials $g(x)$ and $h(x)$ such that
$$
 f(x) f(x+1) = g(h(x+1)).
$$

Let $f(x)$ be a quadratic polynomial. Prove that there exist quadratic polynomials $g(x)$ and $h(x)$ such that
$$
 f(x) f(x^2) = g(h(x)).
$$

positive_text: Determine all integer solutions $(x, y)$ to the equation $2x^2 - 6xy + 3y^2 + 1 = 0$.

negatives.text: Find all pairs of integers $x, y$ such that $2x^2 - 6xy + 3y^2 = 1$.
Find all pairs of integers $x, y$ such that $2x^2 + 6xy + 3y^2 = -1$.
Find all pairs of integers $x, y$ such that $2x^2 - 6xy + 3y^2 = -10$.

positive_text:
Let $ABCD$ be a quadrilateral with perpendicular diagonals intersecting at point $P$. Let $d_{AB}, d_{BC}, d_{CD}, d_{DA}$ denote the perpendicular distances from $P$ to the sides $AB, BC, CD, DA$, respectively. Prove that
$$
\frac{1}{d_{AB}^{2}}+\frac{1}{d_{CD}^{2}}=\frac{1}{d_{BC}^{2}}+\frac{1}{d_{DA}^{2}}
$$

negatives.text:
Let $ABCD$ be a quadrilateral with perpendicular diagonals intersecting at point $P$. Let $h_{1}, h_{2}, h_{3}, h_{4}$ be the lengths of the altitudes from $P$ to $AB, BC, CD, DA$. Show that
$$
\frac{1}{h_{1}}+\frac{1}{h_{3}}=\frac{1}{h_{2}}+\frac{1}{h_{4}}
$$

Let $ABCD$ be a quadrilateral with perpendicular diagonals intersecting at point $P$. Let $h_{1}, h_{2}, h_{3}, h_{4}$ be the lengths of the altitudes from $P$ to $AB, BC, CD, DA$. Show that
$$
\frac{1}{h_{1}^{2}}+\frac{1}{h_{2}^{2}}=\frac{1}{h_{3}^{2}}+\frac{1}{h_{4}^{2}}
$$

Let $ABCD$ be a quadrilateral with perpendicular diagonals intersecting at point $P$. Let $h_{1}, h_{2}, h_{3}, h_{4}$ be the lengths of the altitudes from $P$ to $AB, BC, CD, DA$. Show that
$$
\frac{1}{h_{1}^{2}}+\frac{1}{h_{2}^{2}}=\frac{1}{h_{3}^{2}}-\frac{1}{h_{4}^{2}}
$$

positive_text:
Let $\{a_{n}\}$ and $\{b_{n}\}$ be sequences defined by $a_{0}=2$, $b_{0}=1$ and, for $n \geq 0$,
$$
a_{n+1}=a_{n}^{2}+b_{n}^{2} \quad \text{ and } \quad b_{n+1}=2 a_{n} b_{n}
$$
Derive and prove a closed-form expression for $a_{n}$ in terms of $n$.

negatives.text:
Let $\{x_{n}\}$ and $\{y_{n}\}$ be sequences defined by $x_{0}=2$, $y_{0}=1$ and, for $n \geq 0$,
$$
x_{n+1}=x_{n}^{2}-y_{n}^{2} \quad \text{ and } \quad y_{n+1}=2 x_{n} y_{n}
$$
Find and prove an explicit formula for $x_{n}$ in terms of $n$.

Let $\{x_{n}\}$ and $\{y_{n}\}$ be sequences defined by $x_{0}=2$, $y_{0}=1$ and, for $n \geq 0$,
$$
x_{n+1}=x_{n}^{2}+y_{n}^{2} \quad \text{ and } \quad y_{n+1}=x_{n} y_{n}
$$
Find and prove an explicit formula for $x_{n}$ in terms of $n$.

Let $\{x_{n}\}$ and $\{y_{n}\}$ be sequences defined by $x_{0}=2$, $y_{0}=1$ and, for $n \geq 0$,
$$
x_{n+1}=x_{n}^{2}+2 y_{n}^{2} \quad \text{ and } \quad y_{n+1}=2 x_{n} y_{n}
$$
Find and prove an explicit formula for $x_{n}$ in terms of $n$.

positive_text:
Let $A$ be the number of 4-tuples $(a, b, c, d)$ of positive integers smaller than $N$ such that
$$
 a^{3} + b^{2} = c^{3} + d^{2} + 1,
$$
and let $B$ be the number of 4-tuples $(a, b, c, d)$ of positive integers smaller than $N$ such that
$$
 a^{3} + b^{2} = c^{3} + d^{2}.
$$
Prove that $B > A$.

negatives.text:
